title.zh: 卷一百〇八 志第六十一 禮十一
title.raw: 卷一百〇八 志第六十一 禮十一 Volume 108 Treatises 61: Rites 11

sentences.zh: 禮十一

translations.literal: Rites Eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Rites 11

sentences.zh: （吉禮十一）〉

translations.literal: (Auspicious Rites Eleven) Closing angle bracket.
translations.idiomatic: (Auspicious Rites 11)

sentences.zh: ○時享薦新加上祖宗諡號廟諱

translations.literal: Seasonal offerings, fresh offerings, adding posthumous titles, and temple taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal Offerings, Fresh Offerings, Posthumous Titles, and Temple Taboos

sentences.zh: 時享。

translations.literal: Seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal Offerings

sentences.zh: 太祖乾德六年十月，判太常寺和峴上言：“按《禮閣新儀》，唐天寶五年，詔享太廟宜祭料外，每室加常食一牙盤。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Qiande under Emperor Taizu, He Xian, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, submitted a memorial: "According to the 'New Ritual Compendium of the Ritual Pavilion,' in the fifth year of Tianbao of Tang, an edict ordered that when offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, beyond the sacrificial provisions, each chamber should receive one additional regular meal on a tooth-pattern platter.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Qiande (968), during the reign of Emperor Taizu, He Xian, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, submitted a memorial: "According to the New Ritual Compendium of the Ritual Pavilion, in the fifth year of Tianbao (746) the Tang court decreed that when sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, each ancestral chamber should receive, in addition to the standard sacrificial provisions, one extra regular meal served on a tooth-pattern platter.

sentences.zh: 將來享廟，欲每室加牙盤食，禘祫、時享亦準此製。

translations.literal: For future temple offerings, we wish to add tooth-platter food to each chamber; the di and xia rites and seasonal offerings should likewise follow this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: For future offerings at the temple, we propose adding tooth-platter meals to each chamber, and applying the same rule to the di and xia rites and to seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國六年十二月，太常禮院言：“今月二十三日，臘享太廟。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo under Emperor Taizong, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Affairs stated: "On the twenty-third day of this month, the winter solstice offering will be made at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo (981), during the reign of Emperor Taizong, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Affairs reported: "On the twenty-third of this month the winter solstice offering is scheduled at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 緣孟冬已行時享，冬至又嚐親祀。

translations.literal: Because the early-winter seasonal offering has already been performed, and at the winter solstice the emperor will personally sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The early-winter seasonal offering has already been held, and the emperor is also to perform the personal sacrifice at the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 按禮每歲五享，其禘祫之月即不行時享，慮成煩數，有爽恭虔。

translations.literal: According to ritual, there are five offerings each year; in the months of the di and xia rites seasonal offerings are not performed, lest the ceremonies become too frequent and impair reverent devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual prescribes five offerings per year, and seasonal offerings are omitted in the months of the di and xia rites so that the schedule does not become excessive and undermine solemn devotion.

sentences.zh: 今請罷臘日薦享之禮，其孝惠別廟即如式。

translations.literal: We now request that the winter-solstice fresh-offering rite be abolished; the separate temple of Empress Xiaohui should proceed according to the usual form.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore ask that the winter-solstice fresh-offering ceremony be discontinued, while the separate temple of Empress Xiaohui should follow the established procedure.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年十月八日，太常禮院言：“今年冬至，親祀南郊，前期朝享太廟，及奏告宣祖、太祖室。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the tenth month of the third year of Chunhua, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Affairs stated: "This year at the winter solstice the emperor will personally sacrifice at the Southern Suburb; beforehand he will attend the morning offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and report to the chambers of Emperor Xuanzu and Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the tenth month in the third year of Chunhua (992), the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Affairs reported: "At this year's winter solstice the emperor will personally sacrifice at the Southern Suburb. In advance he will attend the morning offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and present reports at the chambers of Emperor Xuanzu and Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 常例，每遇親祀，設朔、望兩祭，乃是十一月內三祭，太廟兩室 又行奏告之禮，煩則不恭。

translations.literal: By usual practice, whenever there is a personal sacrifice, the new-moon and full-moon offerings are both held, making three ceremonies within the eleventh month; the two chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple also perform the reporting rite — too many rites are indecorous.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, whenever the emperor sacrifices in person, both the new-moon and full-moon offerings are observed, which would mean three ceremonies within November alone; the two ancestral chambers would also undergo the reporting rite. Such frequency would be excessive and lack due reverence.

sentences.zh: 又十一月二十日，皇帝朝享，去臘享日月相隔，未為煩數。

translations.literal: Furthermore, on the twentieth day of the eleventh month the emperor attends the morning offering, separated from the winter-solstice offering by several days — this is not excessively frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the emperor's morning offering on the twentieth of the eleventh month falls several days before the winter-solstice offering and would not be unduly frequent.

sentences.zh: 欲望權停是月朔、望之祭，其臘享如常儀。

translations.literal: We wish provisionally to suspend the new-moon and full-moon offerings of that month; the winter-solstice offering should follow the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: We propose provisionally suspending the new-moon and full-moon offerings for that month, while conducting the winter-solstice offering according to the usual rites.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 真宗景德三年正月，畫日乙卯孟享太廟。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jingde under Emperor Zhenzong, the day was fixed as yimao for the first-month seasonal offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Jingde (1006), during the reign of Emperor Zhenzong, the day yimao was set for the first-month seasonal offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 其日以鄆王外欑，改用辛酉。

translations.literal: On that day, because the Prince of Yun was mourning outside the capital, xinyou was used instead.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Prince of Yun was in mourning outside the capital on that day, the ceremony was moved to xinyou.

sentences.zh: 十月十日，孟冬薦享。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the tenth month, the early-winter fresh offering was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the tenth month the early-winter fresh offering was held.

sentences.zh: 其月，明德皇后園陵，有司言：“故事，大祠與國忌日同日者，其樂備而不作，今請如例。

translations.literal: That month was the anniversary of Empress Mingde's burial; the responsible officials stated: "By precedent, when a major sacrifice falls on the same day as a national mourning anniversary, the music is prepared but not performed; we now request that this precedent be followed.
translations.idiomatic: That month marked the anniversary of Empress Mingde's burial. The responsible officials reported: "By precedent, when a major sacrifice coincides with a national mourning anniversary, the music is prepared but not played. We ask that this precedent be followed.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，以莊穆皇后祔享，權停孟享。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, because Empress Zhuangmu was enshrined in joint worship, the first-month seasonal offering was provisionally suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year (1007), the first-month seasonal offering was provisionally suspended while Empress Zhuangmu was enshrined for joint worship.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年十二月，帝謂王旦等言：“來年正月十一日孟享太廟，而有司擇八日宴，已在享廟致齋中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the emperor said to Wang Dan and others: "Next year the first-month seasonal offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple is set for the eleventh day of the first month, yet the responsible officials have chosen the eighth day for a banquet, which falls within the fasting period before the temple offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1010), the emperor told Wang Dan and the others: "Next year the first-month seasonal offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple is scheduled for the eleventh day of the first month, yet the officials have chosen the eighth for a banquet, which falls within the fasting period before the temple offering.

sentences.zh: 又七日上辛，祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: Furthermore, on the seventh day is the upper xin day for sacrificing to the August Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the seventh is the upper xin day for sacrificing to the August Lord on High.

sentences.zh: ”王欽若言：“若移宴日避祀 事，即自天慶節以來皆有所妨。

translations.literal: " Wang Qinruo said: "If the banquet day is moved to avoid the sacrificial affairs, then from the Tianqing Festival onward there would be conflicts everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo said: "If the banquet is moved to avoid the sacrificial schedule, there would be conflicts from the Tianqing Festival onward.

sentences.zh: ”馮拯言：“上辛不可移，薦享宗廟是有司擇日，於禮無嫌。

translations.literal: " Feng Zheng said: "The upper xin day cannot be moved; the offering at the ancestral temple is a date chosen by the responsible officials, and in ritual terms there is no impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zheng said: "The upper xin day cannot be moved. The ancestral temple offering is a date set by the responsible officials, and there is no ritual impropriety in that.

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“當詢禮官。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The ritual officials should be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The ritual officials should be consulted.

sentences.zh: ”終以契丹使發有常期，又將西巡，故不及改。

translations.literal: " In the end, because the Khitan envoys were to depart on a fixed schedule and the emperor was also about to tour the west, no change was made in time.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, because the Khitan envoys were scheduled to depart on a fixed date and the emperor was also preparing a western tour, no change was made in time.

sentences.zh: 八年，兼宗正卿趙安仁言：“準詔以太廟朔望上食品味，令臣詳定。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Zhao Anren, concurrently director of the Imperial Clan Court, stated: "By imperial decree I am to determine in detail the food items offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple on new-moon and full-moon days.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1015), Zhao Anren, concurrently director of the Imperial Clan Court, reported: "By imperial decree I have been charged with determining the food items offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple on new-moon and full-moon days.

sentences.zh: 望自今委禦廚取親享廟日所上牙盤例，參以四時珍膳，選上局食手十人，赴廟饌造，上副聖心，式表精愨。

translations.literal: I hope that from now on the imperial kitchen may be entrusted to take the tooth-platter offerings presented on days of personal temple sacrifice as the model, supplemented by seasonal delicacies; ten master cooks of the upper bureau should be selected to prepare food at the temple, satisfying the imperial mind and displaying meticulous sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that henceforth the imperial kitchen be instructed to follow the tooth-platter offerings used on days when the emperor sacrifices at the temple, supplemented with seasonal delicacies, and that ten master cooks from the upper bureau be selected to prepare offerings at the temple, thereby meeting the emperor's expectations and demonstrating meticulous devotion.

sentences.zh: ”詔：所上食味，委宮闈令監造訖，安仁省視之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered: The food items to be offered should be entrusted to the director of palace attendants to supervise their preparation; when finished, Anren should inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that preparation of the offerings be supervised by the director of palace attendants, with Anren inspecting them upon completion.

sentences.zh: 神宗元豐三年十月，詳定郊廟奉祀禮文所言：“祠禴嚐蒸之名，春夏則物未成而祭薄，秋冬則物成而禮備。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Shenzong, the commission for determining suburban and temple sacrificial ritual texts stated: "The names ci, yue, chang, and zheng denote that in spring and summer things are not yet ripe and offerings are simple, while in autumn and winter things are ripe and the rites are complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Yuanfeng (1080), during the reign of Emperor Shenzong, the commission for determining suburban and temple sacrificial ritual texts reported: "The terms ci, yue, chang, and zheng reflect that in spring and summer produce is not yet ripe and offerings are modest, whereas in autumn and winter harvests are complete and the rites are fully provisioned.

sentences.zh: 今太廟四時雖有薦新，而孟享禮料無祠禴蒸嚐之別。

translations.literal: Now although the Imperial Ancestral Temple has fresh offerings in all four seasons, the provisions for the first-month seasonal offering make no distinction among ci, yue, zheng, and chang.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Imperial Ancestral Temple already observes fresh offerings in all four seasons, the provisions for the first-month seasonal offering do not distinguish among the ci, yue, zheng, and chang categories.

sentences.zh: 伏 請春加韭、卵，夏加麥、魚，秋加黍、豚，冬加稻、雁，當饋熟之節，薦於神主。

translations.literal: We respectfully request that in spring leeks and eggs be added, in summer wheat and fish, in autumn millet and pork, and in winter rice and geese; at the season when offerings are ripe, they should be presented to the spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully propose adding leeks and eggs in spring, wheat and fish in summer, millet and pork in autumn, and rice and geese in winter, presenting each at the season of ripeness to the spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 其籩豆於常數之外，別加時物之薦，豐約各因其時，以應古禮。

translations.literal: Beyond the usual number of baskets and stands, seasonal offerings should be added separately; abundance or simplicity should follow the season, in accord with ancient ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the usual complement of baskets and stands, seasonal items should be added separately, with abundance or simplicity adjusted to each season in accordance with ancient ritual.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月，帝親祠南郊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year, the emperor personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the sixth year (1083) the emperor personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 前期三日，奉仁宗、英宗徽號冊寶於太廟。

translations.literal: Three days beforehand, the honorific title registers and seals of Emperors Renzong and Yingzong were brought to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Three days in advance, the honorific title registers and seals of Emperors Renzong and Yingzong were conveyed to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 是日，齋於大慶殿。

translations.literal: On that day, he fasted in the Hall of Great Celebration.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor fasted in the Hall of Great Celebration.

sentences.zh: 翌日，薦享於景靈宮。

translations.literal: The next day, a fresh offering was made at the Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The following day a fresh offering was made at the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，乘玉輅至太廟，宰 臣、百官班迎於廟門。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, the emperor wore the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, rode the jade chariot to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the chief ministers and all officials lined up to welcome him at the temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, the emperor donned the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, rode the jade chariot to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the chief ministers and officials formed ranks to welcome him at the temple gate.

sentences.zh: 侍中跪請降輅，帝卻乘輿，步入廟，趍至齋宮。

translations.literal: The palace attendant knelt and requested that he descend from the chariot; the emperor instead boarded the palanquin, entered the temple on foot, and proceeded to the fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendant knelt and asked him to descend from the chariot; the emperor instead entered a palanquin, walked into the temple, and proceeded to the fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝服靴袍至大次。

translations.literal: The next day, the emperor wore boots and robe and proceeded to the great side pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor, wearing boots and robe, proceeded to the great side pavilion.

sentences.zh: 有司奏中嚴、外辦，禮儀使跪奏請行事。

translations.literal: The responsible officials announced the mid-watch strictness and outer preparations; the master of ceremonies knelt and reported, requesting that the rites begin.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials announced the mid-watch strictness and outer preparations, and the master of ceremonies knelt and requested that the rites begin.

sentences.zh: 帝服袞冕以出，至東門外， 殿中監進大圭，帝執以入，宮架樂作，升東階，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the ceremonial robe and crown and came forth; at the outer east gate the director of palace attendants presented the great scepter, which the emperor took and entered; palace ensemble music began; he ascended the east steps and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emerged wearing the ceremonial robe and crown. At the outer east gate the director of palace attendants presented the great scepter, which the emperor took and entered. Palace ensemble music began as he ascended the east steps, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 登歌樂作，至位，樂止。

translations.literal: Ascent music began; when he reached his place, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music began; when he reached his place, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 太祝、宮闈令奉諸室神主於坐，禮儀使讚曰：“有司謹具，請行事。

translations.literal: The grand invoker and the director of palace attendants placed the spirit tablets of all chambers on their seats; the master of ceremonies announced: "The responsible officials have carefully prepared everything; we request that the rites proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The grand invoker and the director of palace attendants placed the spirit tablets of all chambers on their seats. The master of ceremonies announced: "All preparations are complete; we request that the rites proceed.

sentences.zh: ”帝再拜，詣罍 洗，登歌樂作，降階，樂止。

translations.literal: " The emperor bowed twice, proceeded to the wine vessel and wash basin; ascent music began; he descended the steps and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice and proceeded to the wine vessel and wash basin. Ascent music began as he descended the steps, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 宮架樂作，至洗南，北向，樂止。

translations.literal: Palace ensemble music began; he reached the south of the wash basin, faced north, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ensemble music began. He reached the south side of the wash basin, faced north, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝搢圭，盥帨，洗瓚、拭瓚訖，執圭。

translations.literal: The emperor tucked the scepter, washed his hands and dried them, washed and wiped the libation cup, then took the scepter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tucked the scepter in place, washed and dried his hands, washed and wiped the libation cup, then took up the scepter again.

sentences.zh: 宮架樂作，升堂，樂止。

translations.literal: Palace ensemble music began; he ascended the hall and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ensemble music began as he ascended the hall, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 登歌樂作，殿中監進鎮圭。

translations.literal: Ascent music began; the director of palace attendants presented the stabilizing scepter.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music began, and the director of palace attendants presented the stabilizing scepter.

sentences.zh: 帝搢大 圭，執鎮圭，詣僖祖室，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor tucked the great scepter, took the stabilizing scepter, and proceeded to the chamber of Emperor Xizu; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tucked the great scepter in place, took the stabilizing scepter, and proceeded to the chamber of Emperor Xizu; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 登歌奏《瑞安之曲》。

translations.literal: Ascent music performed "The Song of Auspicious Peace."
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music performed "The Song of Auspicious Peace."

sentences.zh: 至神坐前，北向跪，奠鎮圭於繅藉，執大圭跪，三上香，執瓚裸地，奠瓚，奉幣。

translations.literal: Before the spirit seat he knelt facing north, placed the stabilizing scepter on the silk mat, knelt holding the great scepter, offered incense three times, took the libation cup and poured a libation on the ground, set down the cup, and presented the silks.
translations.idiomatic: Before the spirit seat he knelt facing north, placed the stabilizing scepter on the silk mat, knelt holding the great scepter, offered incense three times, poured a libation from the cup onto the ground, set down the cup, and presented the silks.

sentences.zh: 奠訖，執圭，俯伏，興，出 戶外，北向再拜。

translations.literal: When the offerings were complete, he took the scepter, prostrated himself, rose, went outside the door, and bowed twice facing north.
translations.idiomatic: When the offerings were complete, he took the scepter, prostrated himself, rose, went outside the door, and bowed twice facing north.

sentences.zh: 內侍舉鎮圭以授殿中監。

translations.literal: A palace attendant lifted the stabilizing scepter and handed it to the director of palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant lifted the stabilizing scepter and handed it to the director of palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 至次室行事，皆如前儀。

translations.literal: Proceeding to the next chamber to perform the rites, all followed the previous procedure.
translations.idiomatic: At each subsequent chamber the rites were performed according to the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 帝還位，登歌樂作，至位，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to his place; ascent music began; when he reached his place, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to his place. Ascent music began, and when he reached his place the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 宮架《興安之樂》作，文舞九成，止。

translations.literal: The palace ensemble performed "The Music of Rising Peace"; the civil dance was performed nine times, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The palace ensemble performed "The Music of Rising Peace," the civil dance was performed nine times, and then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮部、戶部尚書以次官 奉逐室俎豆，宮架《豐安》樂作，奠訖，樂止。

translations.literal: The ministers of rites and revenue, together with subordinate officials, presented the stands and dishes for each chamber in turn; the palace ensemble performed "Abundant Peace"; when the offerings were complete, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of rites and revenue, together with subordinate officials, presented the stands and dishes for each chamber in turn. The palace ensemble performed "Abundant Peace," and when the offerings were complete the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝再詣罍洗，登歌樂作，降階，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor again proceeded to the wine vessel and wash basin; ascent music began; he descended the steps and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again proceeded to the wine vessel and wash basin. Ascent music began as he descended the steps, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 宮架樂作，至洗南，北向立，樂止。

translations.literal: Palace ensemble music began; he reached the south of the wash basin, stood facing north, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ensemble music began. He reached the south side of the wash basin, stood facing north, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝搢圭，盥帨，洗爵、拭爵訖，執圭。

translations.literal: The emperor tucked the scepter, washed his hands and dried them, washed and wiped the wine cup, then took the scepter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tucked the scepter in place, washed and dried his hands, washed and wiped the wine cup, then took up the scepter again.

sentences.zh: 宮 架樂作，帝升東階，樂止。

translations.literal: Palace ensemble music began; the emperor ascended the east steps and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ensemble music began as the emperor ascended the east steps, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 登歌樂作，至僖祖室，樂止。

translations.literal: Ascent music began; he reached the chamber of Emperor Xizu and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music began. He reached the chamber of Emperor Xizu and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 宮架樂作，帝搢圭跪，受爵，祭酒，三奠爵，執圭，俯伏，興，出戶外，北向立，樂止。

translations.literal: Palace ensemble music began; the emperor tucked the scepter and knelt, received the cup, poured a libation, set down the cup three times, took the scepter, prostrated himself, rose, went outside the door, stood facing north, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ensemble music began. The emperor tucked the scepter and knelt, received the cup, poured a libation, set down the cup three times, took the scepter, prostrated himself, rose, went outside the door, stood facing north, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 太祝讀冊文，帝再 拜。

translations.literal: The grand invoker read the register text; the emperor bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The grand invoker read the register text, and the emperor bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 詣次室，皆如前儀。

translations.literal: Proceeding to the next chamber, all followed the previous procedure.
translations.idiomatic: At each subsequent chamber the rites followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 帝還位，登歌樂作，至位，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to his place; ascent music began; when he reached his place, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to his place. Ascent music began, and when he reached his place the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 文舞退，武舞進，宮架《正安之樂》作，亞獻以次行事如前儀，樂止。

translations.literal: The civil dance withdrew and the military dance advanced; the palace ensemble performed "The Music of Correct Peace"; the secondary presenter performed the rites in turn as before, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance withdrew and the military dance advanced. The palace ensemble performed "The Music of Correct Peace," the secondary presenter performed the rites in turn as before, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝詣飲福位，登歌樂作，至位，樂 止。

translations.literal: The emperor proceeded to the place for drinking the blessing; ascent music began; when he reached his place, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor proceeded to the place for drinking the blessing. Ascent music began, and when he reached his place the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 宮架《僖安》樂作，帝再拜，搢圭跪，受爵，祭酒，三啐酒，奠爵，受俎，奠俎，受摶黍，奠黍豆，再受爵，飲福酒訖，奠爵，執圭，俯伏，興，再拜，樂止。

translations.literal: The palace ensemble performed "The Music of Xizu Peace"; the emperor bowed twice, tucked the scepter and knelt, received the cup, poured a libation, sipped the wine three times, set down the cup, received the stand, set down the stand, received the lump of millet, set down the millet and beans, received the cup again, finished drinking the blessing wine, set down the cup, took the scepter, prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The palace ensemble performed "The Music of Xizu Peace." The emperor bowed twice, tucked the scepter and knelt, received the cup, poured a libation, sipped the wine three times, set down the cup, received the stand and set it down, received the lump of millet and set down the millet and beans, received the cup again and finished drinking the blessing wine, set down the cup, took the scepter, prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝還位，登歌樂作，至位，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to his place; ascent music began; when he reached his place, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to his place. Ascent music began, and when he reached his place the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 太常博士遍祭七祀、配享功臣。

translations.literal: The doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices made offerings throughout to the seven sacrifices and the meritorious officials in joint worship.
translations.idiomatic: The doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices made offerings throughout to the seven sacrifices and the meritorious officials in joint worship.

sentences.zh: 戶部、禮部尚書徹俎豆，登歌《豐安》樂作，徹訖，樂止。

translations.literal: The ministers of revenue and rites removed the stands and dishes; ascent music performed "Abundant Peace"; when removal was complete, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of revenue and rites removed the stands and dishes. Ascent music performed "Abundant Peace," and when removal was complete the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮直官曰“賜胙”，行事、陪祠官皆再 拜，宮架《興安》樂作，一成，止。

translations.literal: The ritual supervisor called out "Bestow the sacrificial meat"; the officiants and attendant worshippers all bowed twice; the palace ensemble performed "Rising Peace," one movement, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual supervisor called out "Bestow the sacrificial meat." The officiants and attendant worshippers all bowed twice. The palace ensemble performed "Rising Peace" for one movement, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 太祝、宮闈令奉神主入諸祏室。

translations.literal: The grand invoker and the director of palace attendants carried the spirit tablets into the spirit-tablet chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The grand invoker and the director of palace attendants carried the spirit tablets into the spirit-tablet chambers.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使跪奏禮畢，登歌樂作，帝降階，樂止。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies knelt and reported that the rites were complete; ascent music began; the emperor descended the steps and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies knelt and reported that the rites were complete. Ascent music began as the emperor descended the steps, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 宮架樂作，出東門，殿中監受大圭，歸大次，樂 止。

translations.literal: Palace ensemble music began; he exited the east gate; the director of palace attendants received the great scepter; he returned to the great side pavilion and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ensemble music began as he exited the east gate. The director of palace attendants received the great scepter, and he returned to the great side pavilion as the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 有司奏解嚴，轉仗赴南郊。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported the lifting of strictness; the guard detachment turned and proceeded to the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials reported the lifting of strictness, and the guard detachment turned and proceeded to the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 初，國朝親享太廟，儀物有制。

translations.literal: Initially, when the dynasty personally offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, ritual objects had fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when the dynasty personally offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, ritual objects followed fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 熙寧以來，率循舊典，元豐命官詳定，始多損益。

translations.literal: From the Xining era onward, old precedents were generally followed; in Yuanfeng officials were ordered to determine the rites in detail, and many additions and reductions began.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xining era onward old precedents were generally followed, but in Yuanfeng officials were ordered to determine the rites in detail, and many revisions were introduced.

sentences.zh: 元年，詳定郊廟禮文所言：“古者納 牲之時，王親執鸞刀，啟其毛，而祝以血毛詔於室。

translations.literal: In the first year, the commission for determining suburban and temple ritual texts stated: "In antiquity, when the sacrificial animal was presented, the king personally held the bell-handled knife, opened the hide, and the invoker presented the blood and hair with an announcement in the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year (1078), the commission for determining suburban and temple ritual texts reported: "In antiquity, when the sacrificial animal was presented, the king personally held the bell-handled knife and opened the hide, while the invoker presented the blood and hair with an announcement in the chamber.

sentences.zh: 今請改正儀注，諸太祝以毛血薦於神坐訖，徹之而退。

translations.literal: We now request correction of the ritual regulations: all grand invokers should present the hair and blood at the spirit seat, and when finished remove them and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: We now request a correction to the ritual regulations: all grand invokers should present the hair and blood at the spirit seat, then remove them and withdraw when finished.

sentences.zh: 唐崔沔議曰：‘毛血盛於盤。

translations.literal: Cui Mian of Tang argued: 'The hair and blood should be placed in a platter.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mian of Tang argued: "The hair and blood should be placed in a platter.

sentences.zh: ’《開元》、《開寶通禮》 及今儀注皆盛以豆。

translations.literal: ' The Comprehensive Rites of Kaiyuan, the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao, and the present ritual regulations all place them in stands.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Rites of Kaiyuan, the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao, and the present ritual regulations all place them in stands.

sentences.zh: 禮以豆盛菹醢，其薦毛血當盛以盤。

translations.literal: Ritual uses stands for pickled vegetables and sauces; presenting hair and blood should use a platter.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual uses stands for pickled vegetables and sauces; hair and blood should be presented in a platter.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“三牲骨體俎外，當加牛羊腸胃、豕膚俎各一。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "Beyond the stands of the three sacrificial animals' bones and flesh, one stand each of ox and sheep intestines and stomach, and pig skin, should be added.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated: "Beyond the stands bearing the bones and flesh of the three sacrificial animals, one stand each of ox and sheep intestines and stomach, and of pig skin, should be added.

sentences.zh: 又古者祭祀無迎神、送神之禮，其初祭及末，皆不 當拜。

translations.literal: Furthermore, in antiquity sacrifices had no rites of welcoming or escorting the spirits; at the initial and final offerings, one should not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, ancient sacrifices had no rites of welcoming or escorting the spirits; bows should not be performed at the initial and final offerings.

sentences.zh: 又宜令戶部陳歲貢以充庭實，如古禮，仍以龜為前，金次之，玉帛又次之，餘居後。

translations.literal: It is also appropriate to order the Ministry of Revenue to display the annual tribute as court offerings, as in ancient ritual: tortoise shells first, gold next, jade and silks after that, and the rest last.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue should also be ordered to display the annual tribute as court offerings, as in ancient ritual: tortoise shells first, then gold, then jade and silks, with the remainder last.

sentences.zh: 又《周禮》大宗伯之職，凡享，蒞玉鬯。

translations.literal: Furthermore, in the "Offices of Zhou," the duty of the grand master of ceremonies is that for all offerings he personally handles the jade libation of aromatic wine.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, in the "Offices of Zhou" the duty of the grand master of ceremonies is that for all offerings he personally handles the jade libation of aromatic wine.

sentences.zh: 今以門下侍郎取瓚進皇帝，侍中 酌鬯進瓚，皆未合禮。

translations.literal: Now the vice director of the Secretariat fetches the libation cup and presents it to the emperor, and the palace attendant pours the aromatic wine and presents the cup — none of this conforms to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At present the vice director of the Secretariat fetches the libation cup and presents it to the emperor, and the palace attendant pours the aromatic wine and presents the cup — none of this conforms to ritual.

sentences.zh: 請命禮部尚書奉瓚臨鬯，禮部侍郎奉槃，以次進，皇帝酌鬯祼地訖，侍郎受瓚並槃而退。

translations.literal: We request that the minister of rites be ordered to hold the libation cup beside the aromatic wine, the vice minister of rites to hold the tray; they should advance in turn; when the emperor has poured the aromatic wine as a libation on the ground, the vice minister should receive the cup and tray together and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: We request that the minister of rites hold the libation cup beside the aromatic wine and the vice minister of rites hold the tray; they should advance in turn. When the emperor has poured the aromatic wine as a libation on the ground, the vice minister should receive the cup and tray together and withdraw.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“皇帝至阼階，乃令太祝、宮闈令始奉神主 置於坐，行禮畢，皇帝俟納神主，然後降階。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "When the emperor reaches the eastern steps, only then should the grand invoker and the director of palace attendants begin to carry the spirit tablets and place them on their seats; when the rites are finished, the emperor should wait until the spirit tablets are stored away before descending the steps.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated: "When the emperor reaches the eastern steps, only then should the grand invoker and the director of palace attendants begin carrying the spirit tablets and placing them on their seats. When the rites are finished, the emperor should wait until the spirit tablets are stored away before descending the steps.

sentences.zh: ”並從之。

translations.literal: " All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 又言：“神坐當陳於室之奧東面。

translations.literal: They also stated: "The spirit seat should be displayed in the inner recess of the chamber, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated: "The spirit seat should be displayed in the inner recess of the chamber, facing east.

sentences.zh: 當行事時，皇帝立於戶內西向，即拜於戶內。

translations.literal: When performing the rites, the emperor should stand inside the door facing west, and bow inside the door.
translations.idiomatic: When performing the rites, the emperor should stand inside the door facing west and bow from within the door.

sentences.zh: 有司攝事，晨祼饋食，亦立於戶內西向，更不出戶而拜。

translations.literal: When officials perform the rites by proxy, for the morning libation and food offering they also stand inside the door facing west, and do not go outside the door to bow.
translations.idiomatic: When officials perform the rites by proxy, for the morning libation and food offering they also stand inside the door facing west and do not go outside to bow.

sentences.zh: 其堂上薦腥，則設神坐於扆前南向，皇帝立於中堂北向。

translations.literal: When raw meat is presented in the hall, the spirit seat should be set before the screen facing south, and the emperor should stand in the central hall facing north.
translations.idiomatic: When raw meat is presented in the hall, the spirit seat should be placed before the screen facing south, with the emperor standing in the central hall facing north.

sentences.zh: 有司攝事同此。

translations.literal: When officials perform the rites by proxy, the same applies.
translations.idiomatic: The same rule applies when officials perform the rites by proxy.

sentences.zh: ”詔俟廟製成取旨。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered that this await completion of the temple construction before receiving imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that this await completion of the temple construction before receiving an imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 又請：“諸廟各設莞筵紛純，加繅席畫純，於戶內之東西面，皇帝行三獻禮畢，於此受嘏。

translations.literal: They also requested: "Each temple should set out rush mats with embroidered borders, topped with painted silk mats with embroidered borders, on the east and west sides inside the door; when the emperor has finished the three offerings, he should receive the blessing here.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested that each temple set out rush mats with embroidered borders, topped with painted silk mats with embroidered borders, on the east and west sides inside the door, and that after the emperor completes the three offerings he receive the blessing there.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“每室所用幾席，當如《周禮》，改用莞筵紛純，加繅席畫 純，加次席黼純，左右玉幾。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "The mats and seats used in each chamber should follow the "Offices of Zhou": rush mats with embroidered borders, topped with painted silk mats with embroidered borders, then secondary mats with ax-pattern borders, with jade armrests on left and right.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated that the mats and seats used in each chamber should follow the "Offices of Zhou": rush mats with embroidered borders, topped with painted silk mats with embroidered borders, then secondary mats with ax-pattern borders, with jade armrests on left and right.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀，皆繅次各加一重，並莞筵一重為五重。

translations.literal: For all sacrifices, each painted and secondary layer adds one tier, together with one rush-mat tier making five tiers in all.
translations.idiomatic: For all sacrifices, each painted and secondary layer adds one tier, together with one rush-mat tier for five tiers in all.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“古者宗廟九獻，皇及後各四，諸臣一。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "In antiquity the ancestral temple had nine offerings: the emperor and empress four each, and the ministers one.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated that in antiquity the ancestral temple had nine offerings: the emperor and empress four each, and the ministers one.

sentences.zh: 自漢以來為三獻，後無入廟之事，沿 襲至今。

translations.literal: Since Han there have been three offerings; the empress no longer enters the temple, and this has continued to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han there have been three offerings; the empress no longer enters the temple, and this practice has continued to the present.

sentences.zh: 若時享則有事於室，而無事於堂；

translations.literal: For seasonal offerings there are rites in the chamber but none in the hall;
translations.idiomatic: For seasonal offerings there are rites in the chamber but none in the hall;

sentences.zh: 禘祫則有事於堂，而無事於室。

translations.literal: for the di and xia rites there are rites in the hall but none in the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: for the di and xia rites there are rites in the hall but none in the chamber.

sentences.zh: 室中神位不在奧，堂上神位不當扆，有饋食而無朝踐。

translations.literal: The spirit seat in the chamber is not in the inner recess; the spirit seat in the hall is not before the screen; there is a food offering but no morning presentation of raw meat.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit seat in the chamber is not placed in the inner recess; the spirit seat in the hall is not placed before the screen; there is a food offering but no morning presentation of raw meat.

sentences.zh: 度今之宜，以備古九獻之意，請室 中設神位於奧東面，堂上設神位於戶外之西南面，皇帝立於戶內西南，祼鬯為一獻；

translations.literal: Considering what is suitable today, to preserve the meaning of the ancient nine offerings, we request that in the chamber the spirit seat be set in the inner recess facing east; in the hall the spirit seat be set outside the door on the southwest side; the emperor should stand inside the door on the southwest; pouring the aromatic wine libation counts as the first offering;
translations.idiomatic: Considering what is suitable today and to preserve the meaning of the ancient nine offerings, we request that in the chamber the spirit seat be placed in the inner recess facing east, in the hall the spirit seat be placed outside the door on the southwest side, the emperor stand inside the door on the southwest, and pouring the aromatic wine libation count as the first offering;

sentences.zh: 出戶立於扆前，北向，行朝踐薦腥之禮為再獻；

translations.literal: going outside the door to stand before the screen facing north and performing the morning presentation of raw meat counts as the second offering;
translations.idiomatic: going outside the door to stand before the screen facing north and performing the morning presentation of raw meat counts as the second offering;

sentences.zh: 皇帝立於戶內西面，行饋食薦熟 之禮為三獻。

translations.literal: the emperor standing inside the door facing west and performing the food offering of cooked meat counts as the third offering.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor standing inside the door facing west and performing the food offering of cooked meat counts as the third offering.

sentences.zh: ”詔並候廟製成取旨。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered that all await completion of the temple construction before receiving imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that all of these await completion of the temple construction before receiving an imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 又請：“三年親祠，並祫享及有司攝事，每室並用太牢及製幣。

translations.literal: They also requested: "For the triennial personal sacrifice, the xia offering, and rites performed by officials by proxy, each chamber should use the grand sacrificial victim and prepared silks.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested that for the triennial personal sacrifice, the xia offering, and rites performed by officials by proxy, each chamber use the grand sacrificial victim and prepared silks.

sentences.zh: 宗廟堂上蕭以求陽，而有司行事茅香，宜 易用蕭。

translations.literal: In the ancestral temple hall mugwort is taken to seek yang, but the officials conducting the rite take fragrant grass; mugwort should be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: In the ancestral temple hall mugwort is taken to seek yang, but the officials conducting the rite use fragrant grass; mugwort should be used instead.

sentences.zh: 灌鬯於地以求陰，宜束茅沃酒以象神之飲。

translations.literal: Pouring aromatic wine on the ground seeks yin; bundled rush should be moistened with wine to represent the spirit's drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Pouring aromatic wine on the ground seeks yin; bundled rush should be moistened with wine to represent the spirit's drinking.

sentences.zh: 凡幣皆埋於西階東，冊則藏有司之匱。

translations.literal: All silks should be buried east of the west steps; registers should be stored in the officials' chest.
translations.idiomatic: All silks should be buried east of the west steps, and registers stored in the officials' chest.

sentences.zh: ”又請：“除去殿下板位及小次，而設皇帝板位於東階之上，西向。

translations.literal: " They also requested: "Remove the mat seats below the hall and the small side pavilion, and set the emperor's mat seat on top of the east steps, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested removal of the mat seats below the hall and the small side pavilion, and that the emperor's mat seat be set on top of the east steps, facing west.

sentences.zh: ”又 請：“凡奏告、祈禱、報謝，用牲牢祭饌，並出帝後神主，以明天地一體之義。

translations.literal: " They also requested: "For all reports, prayers, and thanksgiving offerings, use sacrificial victims and offerings, and bring out the spirit tablets of the emperor and empress, to clarify the principle that Heaven and Earth are one body.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested that for all reports, prayers, and thanksgiving offerings, sacrificial victims and offerings be used and the spirit tablets of the emperor and empress brought out, to clarify the principle that Heaven and Earth form one body.

sentences.zh: 又古者祭祀，兼薦上古、中古及當世之食，唐天寶中，始詔薦享每室加常食一牙盤， 議者以為宴私之饌可薦寢宮，而不可瀆於太廟，宜罷之。

translations.literal: Furthermore, in antiquity sacrifices presented food from high antiquity, middle antiquity, and the present age; in the Tianbao era of Tang, an edict first ordered that each chamber in fresh offerings receive one tooth-platter of regular food; critics held that private banquet fare might be offered in the sleeping palace but should not profane the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and it should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, in antiquity sacrifices presented food from high antiquity, middle antiquity, and the present age. In the Tianbao era of Tang an edict first ordered that each chamber in fresh offerings receive one tooth-platter of regular food. Critics held that private banquet fare might be offered in the sleeping palace but should not profane the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and that it should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 古者吉祭必以其妃配，不特拜，請奠副爵無特拜。

translations.literal: In antiquity auspicious sacrifices always paired the consort; there was no separate bow; we request that setting down the secondary cup require no separate bow.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity auspicious sacrifices always paired the consort without a separate bow. We request that setting down the secondary cup require no separate bow.

sentences.zh: 《儀禮》曰：‘嗣舉奠。

translations.literal: The "Ceremonial Rituals" states: 'The heir raises the offering.
translations.idiomatic: The "Ceremonial Rituals" states: "The heir raises the offering.

sentences.zh: ’請皇帝祭太廟，既稞之後，太 祝以斝酌奠於鉶之南，俟正祭嘏訖，命皇子舉奠而飲。

translations.literal: ' We request that when the emperor sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, after the libation the grand invoker pour from the jia cup and set the offering south of the meat stand; when the main sacrifice and blessing are finished, order the imperial prince to raise the offering and drink.
translations.idiomatic: We request that when the emperor sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, after the libation the grand invoker pour from the jia cup and set the offering south of the meat stand; when the main sacrifice and blessing are finished, the imperial prince should be ordered to raise the offering and drink.

sentences.zh: 又請：“命刑部尚書一員以奉大牲，兵部尚書一員奉魚十有五。

translations.literal: They also requested: "Order one minister of punishments to present the grand sacrificial victim, and one minister of war to present fifteen fish.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested that one minister of punishments be ordered to present the grand sacrificial victim and one minister of war to present fifteen fish.

sentences.zh: 仍令腥熟之薦，朝享、及四 孟、臘享，皆設神位於戶內南向。

translations.literal: Furthermore, for presentations of raw and cooked meat, morning offerings, the four first-month offerings, and winter-solstice offerings, spirit seats should all be set inside the door facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, for presentations of raw and cooked meat, morning offerings, the four first-month offerings, and winter-solstice offerings, spirit seats should all be set inside the door facing south.

sentences.zh: 其祼將於室，朝踐於堂，饋熟於室，則於奧設莞筵紛純，加繅席畫純，加次席黼純，左右玉幾。

translations.literal: When the libation is poured in the chamber, raw meat is presented in the hall, and cooked food is offered in the chamber, then in the inner recess set rush mats with embroidered borders, topped with painted silk mats with embroidered borders, then secondary mats with ax-pattern borders, with jade armrests on left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When the libation is poured in the chamber, raw meat presented in the hall, and cooked food offered in the chamber, rush mats with embroidered borders should be set in the inner recess, topped with painted silk mats with embroidered borders, then secondary mats with ax-pattern borders, with jade armrests on left and right.

sentences.zh: 當筵前，設饋食之豆八，加豆八， 以南為上。

translations.literal: Before the mat, set eight stands for food offerings and eight additional stands, with the south as the place of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mat, set eight stands for food offerings and eight additional stands, with the south as the place of honor.

sentences.zh: 鉶三，設於豆之南。

translations.literal: Three meat stands, set south of the stands.
translations.idiomatic: Three meat stands should be set south of the stands.

sentences.zh: 南陳牛鉶居北，羊鉶在牛鉶之南，豕鉶在羊鉶之南。

translations.literal: Arranged from the south: the ox stand is northernmost, the sheep stand south of the ox stand, and the pig stand south of the sheep stand.
translations.idiomatic: Arranged from the south: the ox stand is northernmost, the sheep stand south of the ox stand, and the pig stand south of the sheep stand.

sentences.zh: 羞豆二，曰酏食、糝食，設於薦豆之北。

translations.literal: Two delicacy stands, called fermented-milk food and powdered food, set north of the presentation stands.
translations.idiomatic: Two delicacy stands, called fermented-milk food and powdered food, should be set north of the presentation stands.

sentences.zh: 大羹湆盛以登，設於羞豆之北。

translations.literal: Great broth and meat broth are placed in elevated vessels and set north of the delicacy stands.
translations.idiomatic: Great broth and meat broth should be placed in elevated vessels and set north of the delicacy stands.

sentences.zh: 九俎設 於豆之東，三三為列，以南為上。

translations.literal: Nine meat stands are set east of the stands, arranged in rows of three, with the south as the place of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Nine meat stands should be set east of the stands, arranged in rows of three, with the south as the place of honor.

sentences.zh: 肵俎一，當臘俎之北，縱設之。

translations.literal: One viscera stand, placed north of the cured-meat stand, set lengthwise.
translations.idiomatic: One viscera stand should be placed north of the cured-meat stand, set lengthwise.

sentences.zh: 牲首俎在北牖下，簠簋設於俎南，西上。

translations.literal: The sacrificial-head stand is below the north window; grain vessels are set south of the stands, with the west uppermost.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial-head stand is below the north window; grain vessels should be set south of the stands, with the west uppermost.

sentences.zh: 籩十有八，設於簠簋之南，北上。

translations.literal: Eighteen baskets are set south of the grain vessels, with the north uppermost.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen baskets should be set south of the grain vessels, with the north uppermost.

sentences.zh: 戶外之東設尊彝，西 上，南肆。

translations.literal: East of the outside of the door set ritual wine vessels; west uppermost, displayed toward the south.
translations.idiomatic: East of the outside of the door ritual wine vessels should be set, west uppermost, displayed toward the south.

sentences.zh: 胙階之東設六罍，其三在西，以盛玄酒，其三在東，以盛三酒。

translations.literal: East of the sacrificial-meat steps set six wine jars: three on the west to hold clear water, three on the east to hold the three wines.
translations.idiomatic: East of the sacrificial-meat steps six wine jars should be set: three on the west to hold clear water and three on the east to hold the three wines.

sentences.zh: 堂下陳鼎之位，在東序之南，居洗之西，皆西面北上。

translations.literal: Positions for cauldrons below the hall are south of the east corridor, west of the wash basin, all facing west with the north uppermost.
translations.idiomatic: Positions for cauldrons below the hall should be south of the east corridor and west of the wash basin, all facing west with the north uppermost.

sentences.zh: 匕皆加於鼎之東，俎皆設於鼎之 西，西肆。

translations.literal: Spoons are all placed east of the cauldrons; stands are all set west of the cauldrons, displayed toward the west.
translations.idiomatic: Spoons should all be placed east of the cauldrons and stands set west of the cauldrons, displayed toward the west.

sentences.zh: 肵俎在北，亦西肆。

translations.literal: The viscera stand is on the north, also displayed toward the west.
translations.idiomatic: The viscera stand is on the north, also displayed toward the west.

sentences.zh: 若廟門外，則陳鼎於東方，各當其鑊，而在其鑊之西，皆北面北上。

translations.literal: If outside the temple gate, then set cauldrons in the east, each aligned with its cooking pot and west of its pot, all facing north with the north uppermost.
translations.idiomatic: If outside the temple gate, cauldrons should be set in the east, each aligned with its cooking pot and west of its pot, all facing north with the north uppermost.

sentences.zh: 又請：“既晨祼，諸太祝入，以血毛奠神坐。

translations.literal: They also requested: "After the morning libation, all grand invokers enter and present blood and hair at the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested that after the morning libation all grand invokers enter and present blood and hair at the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 太 官令取肝，以鸞刀製之，洗於鬱鬯，貫以膋，燎於爐炭。

translations.literal: The director of the imperial kitchen takes the liver, prepares it with the bell-handled knife, washes it in aromatic wine, threads it with fat, and burns it on charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the imperial kitchen takes the liver, prepares it with the bell-handled knife, washes it in aromatic wine, threads it with fat, and burns it on charcoal.

sentences.zh: 祝以肝膋入，詔神於室，又出以隋祭於戶外之左，三祭於茅菹。

translations.literal: The invoker enters with the liver and fat, announces to the spirit in the chamber, then goes out and performs the sui offering to the left outside the door, making three offerings on the rush and pickled vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker enters with the liver and fat and announces to the spirit in the chamber, then goes out and performs the sui offering to the left outside the door, making three offerings on the rush and pickled vegetables.

sentences.zh: 當饋熟之時，祝取菹擩於醢，祭於神坐前， 豆間三。

translations.literal: When cooked food is offered, the invoker takes pickled vegetables dipped in sauce and offers them before the spirit seat, three times between the stands.
translations.idiomatic: When cooked food is offered, the invoker takes pickled vegetables dipped in sauce and offers them before the spirit seat, three times between the stands.

sentences.zh: 又取黍稷肺祭，祭如初，藉以白茅。

translations.literal: He also takes millet, glutinous millet, and lung for offering, offering as before on white rush.
translations.idiomatic: He also takes millet, glutinous millet, and lung for offering, offering as before on white rush.

sentences.zh: 既祭，宮闈令束而瘞之於西階東。

translations.literal: After the offering, the director of palace attendants bundles them and buries them east of the west steps.
translations.idiomatic: After the offering, the director of palace attendants bundles them and buries them east of the west steps.

sentences.zh: 若郊祀天地，則當進熟之時，祝取菹及黍稷肺，祭於正配神坐前，各三祭，畢，郊社 令束茅菹而燔瘞之。

translations.literal: If sacrificing to Heaven and Earth at the suburb, then when the cooked offering is presented, the invoker takes pickled vegetables and millet, glutinous millet, and lung and offers them before the principal and associated spirit seats, three offerings each; when finished, the director of suburban and altar rites bundles the rush and pickled vegetables and burns or buries them.
translations.idiomatic: If sacrificing to Heaven and Earth at the suburb, then when the cooked offering is presented the invoker takes pickled vegetables and millet, glutinous millet, and lung and offers them before the principal and associated spirit seats, three offerings each; when finished the director of suburban and altar rites bundles the rush and pickled vegetables and burns or buries them.

sentences.zh: 祀天燔，祭地瘞，縮酒之茅，或燔或瘞，當與隋祭之菹同。

translations.literal: For Heaven sacrifice, burn; for Earth sacrifice, bury; the rush for filtering wine may be burned or buried, and should be the same as the pickled vegetables for the sui offering.
translations.idiomatic: For Heaven sacrifice, burn; for Earth sacrifice, bury. The rush for filtering wine may be burned or buried and should be treated the same as the pickled vegetables for the sui offering.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“古者吉祭有配，皆一屍。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "In antiquity auspicious sacrifices with a consort all had one impersonator.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated that in antiquity auspicious sacrifices with a consort all had one impersonator.

sentences.zh: 其始祝洗酌奠，奠於鉶南，止有一爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning the invoker washed, poured, and set the offering south of the meat stand — there was only one cup.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning the invoker washed, poured, and set the offering south of the meat stand — there was only one cup.

sentences.zh: 及主人獻 屍，主婦亞獻，賓長三獻，亦止一爵。

translations.literal: When the host presented to the impersonator, the hostess made the secondary presentation, and the chief guest the third presentation, there was also only one cup.
translations.idiomatic: When the host presented to the impersonator, the hostess made the secondary presentation, and the chief guest the third presentation, there was also only one cup.

sentences.zh: 請罷諸室奠副爵。

translations.literal: We request abolishing the secondary cups set down in all chambers.
translations.idiomatic: We request abolishing the secondary cups set down in all chambers.

sentences.zh: 其祫享別廟，皇后自如常禮。

translations.literal: For the xia offering at separate temples, the empress follows the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: For the xia offering at separate temples, the empress follows the usual rites.

sentences.zh: 應祠告天地、宗廟、社稷，並用牲幣。

translations.literal: Sacrifices reporting to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain should all use sacrificial victims and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices reporting to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain should all use sacrificial victims and silks.

sentences.zh: 如唐置太廟局令，以宗正丞充，罷攝知 廟少卿，而宮闈令不預祠事。

translations.literal: As Tang established a director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple bureau, filled by the vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, abolish the acting vice director of the temple, and the director of palace attendants should not participate in sacrificial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Tang established a director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple bureau, filled by the vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, the acting vice director of the temple should be abolished, and the director of palace attendants should not participate in sacrificial affairs.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“晨祼之時，皇帝先搢大圭，上香、祼鬯、復位，候作樂饋食畢，再搢大圭，執鎮圭，奠於繅藉。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "At the morning libation, the emperor first tucks the great scepter, offers incense, pours the aromatic wine libation, and returns to his place; when the music and food offering are finished, he again tucks the great scepter, takes the stabilizing scepter, and sets it on the silk mat.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated that at the morning libation the emperor first tucks the great scepter, offers incense, pours the aromatic wine libation, and returns to his place; when the music and food offering are finished he again tucks the great scepter, takes the stabilizing scepter, and sets it on the silk mat.

sentences.zh: 次奠幣、執爵，庶禮神並在 降神之後。

translations.literal: Next setting down silks and taking the cup — all rites honoring the spirit should come after the descent of the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Next setting down silks and taking the cup — all rites honoring the spirit should come after the descent of the spirit.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，太常寺言：“故事，山陵前，宗廟輟祭享，朔望以內臣行薦食之禮，俟祔廟畢仍舊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices stated: "By precedent, before the imperial tomb is completed, the ancestral temple suspends sacrificial offerings; on new-moon and full-moon days inner officials perform the fresh-food offering rite; when enshrinement in the temple is complete, the old practice resumes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "By precedent, before the imperial tomb is completed the ancestral temple suspends sacrificial offerings; on new-moon and full-moon days inner officials perform the fresh-food offering rite; when enshrinement in the temple is complete the old practice resumes.

sentences.zh: 今景靈宮神禦殿已行上食，太廟朔望薦食自當請罷。

translations.literal: Now the Spirit Imperial Hall of the Jingling Palace already performs food offerings; the Imperial Ancestral Temple's new-moon and full-moon fresh offerings should naturally be requested to cease.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Spirit Imperial Hall of the Jingling Palace already performs food offerings, the Imperial Ancestral Temple's new-moon and full-moon fresh offerings should be discontinued.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 元祐七年，詔復用牙盤食。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanyou, an edict restored the use of tooth-platter food.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanyou (1092) an edict restored the use of tooth-platter food.

sentences.zh: 舊制，並於禮饌外設，元豐中罷之，禮官呂希純建議曰：“先王之祭，皆備上古、中古及今世之食。

translations.literal: By old regulation, it was set out beyond the ritual provisions; in Yuanfeng it was abolished. The ritual official Lü Xichun proposed: "The sacrifices of the former kings all provided food from high antiquity, middle antiquity, and the present age.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation it was set out beyond the ritual provisions; in Yuanfeng it was abolished. The ritual official Lü Xichun proposed: "The sacrifices of the former kings all provided food from high antiquity, middle antiquity, and the present age.

sentences.zh: 所設禮饌，即上古、中古之食，牙 盤常食，即今世之食。

translations.literal: The ritual provisions set out are food from high and middle antiquity; tooth-platter regular food is food of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual provisions set out are food from high and middle antiquity; tooth-platter regular food is food of the present age.

sentences.zh: 議者乃以為宗廟牙盤原於秦、漢陵寢上食，殊不知三代以來，自備古今之食。

translations.literal: Critics held that the ancestral temple tooth-platter originated from Qin and Han tomb food offerings, not knowing that since the Three Dynasties food from past and present has always been provided.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that the ancestral temple tooth-platter originated from Qin and Han tomb food offerings, not knowing that since the Three Dynasties food from past and present has always been provided.

sentences.zh: 請依祖宗舊制，薦一牙盤。

translations.literal: We request following the old regulation of the ancestors and presenting one tooth-platter.
translations.idiomatic: We request following the old regulation of the ancestors and presenting one tooth-platter.

sentences.zh: ”從之，乃更其名曰薦羞。

translations.literal: " The request was approved, and the name was changed to "fresh delicacies."
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved, and the name was changed to "fresh delicacies."

sentences.zh: 希純又 請：“帝後各奠一爵，後爵謂之副爵。

translations.literal: Xichun also requested: "The emperor and empress each set down one cup; the empress's cup is called the secondary cup.
translations.idiomatic: Xichun also requested that the emperor and empress each set down one cup, the empress's cup being called the secondary cup.

sentences.zh: 今帝後惟奠一爵共享，瀆禮莫甚。

translations.literal: Now the emperor and empress set down only one cup to share — nothing profanes ritual more.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor and empress set down only one cup to share — nothing profanes ritual more.

sentences.zh: 請設副爵，亦如其儀。

translations.literal: We request setting out a secondary cup, following the same procedure.
translations.idiomatic: We request setting out a secondary cup according to the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 大觀四年，議禮局言：“太廟每享，各設太尊二，則 是以追享、朝享之尊，施之於禴祠蒸嚐，失禮尤甚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daguan, the Ritual Deliberation Bureau stated: "At each offering in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, two grand wine vessels are set — applying the vessels of posthumous and morning offerings to the yue, ci, zheng, and chang sacrifices is a grave breach of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daguan (1110) the Ritual Deliberation Bureau reported: "At each offering in the Imperial Ancestral Temple two grand wine vessels are set — applying the vessels of posthumous and morning offerings to the yue, ci, zheng, and chang sacrifices is a grave breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 請今四時之享，不設太尊。

translations.literal: We request that for the four-season offerings, grand wine vessels not be set.
translations.idiomatic: We request that grand wine vessels not be set for the four-season offerings.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“圭瓚之製，親祀以塗金銀瓚，有司行事以銅瓚，其大小長短之製皆不如 禮，請改以應古製。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "For the scepter and libation cup, personal sacrifice uses gold- and silver-plated cups, and rites performed by officials use bronze cups; their sizes and dimensions all fall short of ritual — we request changing them to conform to ancient regulations.
