We request changing them to conform to ancient regulations.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“太廟圭瓚、別廟璋瓚，舊用瑉石，請改用玉。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "The Imperial Ancestral Temple scepter and libation cup and the separate temple scepter and libation cup formerly used min stone; we request changing to jade.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated that the Imperial Ancestral Temple scepter and libation cup and the separate temple scepter and libation cup formerly used min stone and should be changed to jade.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“新定太廟陳設之儀，盡依周製，籩豆各用二十有六，簠簋各八。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "The newly fixed arrangement for the Imperial Ancestral Temple follows Zhou regulations entirely: baskets and stands each use twenty-six, grain vessels each eight.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated that the newly fixed arrangement for the Imperial Ancestral Temple follows Zhou regulations entirely: baskets and stands each use twenty-six, grain vessels each eight.

sentences.zh: 以籩二十有 六為四行，以右為上，羞籩二為第一行，朝事籩八次之，饋食籩八又次之，加籩八又次之。

translations.literal: The twenty-six baskets form four rows, with the right as the place of honor: two delicacy baskets in the first row, eight morning-affairs baskets next, eight food-offering baskets next, and eight additional baskets last.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-six baskets form four rows, with the right as the place of honor: two delicacy baskets in the first row, eight morning-affairs baskets next, eight food-offering baskets next, and eight additional baskets last.

sentences.zh: 豆二十有六為四行，以左為上，羞豆二為第一行，朝事豆八次之，饋食豆 八又次之，加豆八又次之。

translations.literal: The twenty-six stands form four rows, with the left as the place of honor: two delicacy stands in the first row, eight morning-affairs stands next, eight food-offering stands next, and eight additional stands last.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-six stands form four rows, with the left as the place of honor: two delicacy stands in the first row, eight morning-affairs stands next, eight food-offering stands next, and eight additional stands last.

sentences.zh: 簠八為二行，在籩之外，簋八為二行，在豆之外。

translations.literal: Eight grain vessels form two rows outside the baskets; eight grain vessels form two rows outside the stands.
translations.idiomatic: Eight grain vessels form two rows outside the baskets, and eight grain vessels form two rows outside the stands.

sentences.zh: 籩豆所實之物，悉如《周禮》籩人、醢人之製，惟簠以稻粱，簋以黍稷，而茅菹以蓴， 蚳醢以蜂子代之。

translations.literal: The items placed in baskets and stands all follow the regulations of the basket-keeper and sauce-keeper in the "Offices of Zhou"; only the grain vessels hold rice and millet, the grain bowls hold millet and glutinous millet, rush pickles use water shield, and larva sauce uses bee larvae as substitute.
translations.idiomatic: The items placed in baskets and stands all follow the regulations of the basket-keeper and sauce-keeper in the "Offices of Zhou"; grain vessels hold rice and millet, grain bowls hold millet and glutinous millet, rush pickles use water shield, and larva sauce uses bee larvae as substitute.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“宗廟之祭用太牢而三鉶，實牛、羊、豕之羹，固無可論者。

translations.literal: " They also stated: "The ancestral temple sacrifice uses the grand victim with three meat stands filled with ox, sheep, and pig broth — this is beyond dispute.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated that the ancestral temple sacrifice uses the grand victim with three meat stands filled with ox, sheep, and pig broth — this is beyond dispute.

sentences.zh: 至於太羹止設一登，以《少牢饋食禮》考之，則少牢者羊、豕之牲也。

translations.literal: As for the great broth, only one elevated vessel is set; examining the "Lesser Victim Food-Offering Rite," the lesser victim is sheep and pig.
translations.idiomatic: As for the great broth, only one elevated vessel is set; examining the "Lesser Victim Food-Offering Rite," the lesser victim is sheep and pig.

sentences.zh: 佐食 羞兩鉶，司士進湆二豆。

translations.literal: The assistant presenter offers two meat stands as delicacies; the steward presents two stands of meat broth.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant presenter offers two meat stands as delicacies, and the steward presents two stands of meat broth.

sentences.zh: 三牲之祭，鉶既設三，則登亦如其數。

translations.literal: For the three-victim sacrifice, since three meat stands are set, the elevated vessels should likewise be three.
translations.idiomatic: For the three-victim sacrifice, since three meat stands are set, the elevated vessels should likewise be three.

sentences.zh: 請太廟設三登，實牛、羊、豕之湆以為太羹，明堂亦如之。

translations.literal: We request that the Imperial Ancestral Temple set three elevated vessels filled with ox, sheep, and pig broth as great broth; the Bright Hall should likewise.
translations.idiomatic: We request that the Imperial Ancestral Temple set three elevated vessels filled with ox, sheep, and pig broth as great broth, and that the Bright Hall do likewise.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎三年，奉安神主 於溫州，權用酒脯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan under Emperor Gaozong, the spirit tablets were enshrined at Wenzhou; wine and dried meat were used provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan (1129), during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, the spirit tablets were enshrined at Wenzhou, and wine and dried meat were used provisionally.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，臨安府建太廟，始用特羊，十年改用少牢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, when Lin'an Prefecture built the Imperial Ancestral Temple, a single sheep was first used; in the tenth year the lesser victim was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxing (1135), when Lin'an Prefecture built the Imperial Ancestral Temple, a single sheep was first used; in the tenth year (1140) the lesser victim was adopted.

sentences.zh: 其廟享之禮，七年祀明堂於建康，以徽宗之喪，太常少卿吳表臣援熙寧故事，謂當英宗喪 未除，不廢景靈宮、太廟之禮。

translations.literal: Regarding the temple offering rites: in the seventh year the Bright Hall was sacrificed to at Jiankang; because of Emperor Huizong's mourning, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wu Biaochen cited the Xining precedent, saying that when Emperor Yingzong's mourning had not yet ended, the rites of the Jingling Palace and Imperial Ancestral Temple were not suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the temple offering rites: in the seventh year (1137) the Bright Hall was sacrificed to at Jiankang. Because of Emperor Huizong's mourning, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wu Biaochen cited the Xining precedent, noting that when Emperor Yingzong's mourning had not yet ended, the rites of the Jingling Palace and Imperial Ancestral Temple were not suspended.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士朱震以為不然，謂：“《王製》：‘喪三年不祭，惟天地、社稷越紼行事。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Zhu Zhen disagreed, stating: "The 'Royal Regulations' says: 'During three years of mourning one does not sacrifice; only to Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain does one proceed wearing the mourning sash.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Zhu Zhen disagreed, citing the "Royal Regulations": "During three years of mourning one does not sacrifice; only to Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain does one proceed wearing the mourning sash.

sentences.zh: ’孰謂三年之喪，而可以見宗廟行吉禮乎？

translations.literal: ' Who would say that during three years of mourning one may attend the ancestral temple and perform auspicious rites?
translations.idiomatic: Who would say that during three years of mourning one may attend the ancestral temple and perform auspicious rites?

sentences.zh: ”吏 部尚書孫近等言：“按《春秋》：‘君薨，卒哭而祔，祔而作主，特祀於寢，蒸嚐禘於廟。

translations.literal: " Minister of Personnel Sun Jin and others stated: "According to the "Spring and Autumn Annals": 'When the ruler dies, after the end-of-mourning wailing he is enshrined; upon enshrinement a tablet is made; he receives special sacrifice in the sleeping palace, while zheng, chang, and di are in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Sun Jin and others stated, citing the "Spring and Autumn Annals": "When the ruler dies, after the end-of-mourning wailing he is enshrined; upon enshrinement a tablet is made; he receives special sacrifice in the sleeping palace, while zheng, chang, and di are in the temple.

sentences.zh: ’杜預謂：“新主既特祀於寢，則宗廟常祀，自當如舊。

translations.literal: ' Du Yu said: 'Since the new tablet already receives special sacrifice in the sleeping palace, regular ancestral temple sacrifices should naturally continue as before.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu said: "Since the new tablet already receives special sacrifice in the sleeping palace, regular ancestral temple sacrifices should naturally continue as before.

sentences.zh: ’又熙寧元年， 神宗諒暗，用景德故事，躬行郊廟之禮。

translations.literal: ' Furthermore, in the first year of Xining, during Emperor Shenzong's mourning seclusion, the Jingde precedent was used and he personally performed the suburban and temple rites.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, in the first year of Xining (1068), during Emperor Shenzong's mourning seclusion, the Jingde precedent was used and he personally performed the suburban and temple rites.

sentences.zh: 今明堂大禮，已在以日易月服除之後，皇帝合享太廟，所有鹵簿、鼓吹及樓前宮架、諸軍音樂皆備而不作。

translations.literal: Now the Bright Hall grand rite falls after the end of mourning when days replace months; the emperor should jointly offer at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; all guard of honor, drums and pipes, palace ensemble before the tower, and military band music should be prepared but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Bright Hall grand rite falls after the end of mourning when days replace months. The emperor should jointly offer at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and all guard of honor, drums and pipes, palace ensemble before the tower, and military band music should be prepared but not performed.

sentences.zh: 薦新。

translations.literal: Fresh offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh Offerings

sentences.zh: 太宗雍熙二年十一月，宗正寺言：“準詔，送兔十頭充享太廟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Yongxi under Emperor Taizong, the Imperial Clan Court stated: "By imperial decree, ten rabbits are sent to serve for offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Yongxi (985), during the reign of Emperor Taizong, the Imperial Clan Court reported: "By imperial decree, ten rabbits are sent to serve for offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 按《開寶通禮》，薦新之儀，詣僖祖室戶前，盥洗酌獻訖，再拜， 次獻諸室如上禮。

translations.literal: According to the "Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao," the fresh-offering rite proceeds to the door of Emperor Xizu's chamber, washes hands, pours and presents the offering, bows twice, then presents to the other chambers following the same rite.
translations.idiomatic: According to the "Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao," the fresh-offering rite proceeds to the door of Emperor Xizu's chamber; after washing hands, pouring, and presenting the offering, one bows twice, then presents to the other chambers following the same rite.

sentences.zh: ”遂詔曰：“夫順時蒐狩，禮有舊章，非樂畋遊，將薦宗廟，久隳前製，闕孰甚焉。

translations.literal: " An edict then stated: "Seasonal hunting follows old regulations in ritual; this is not pleasure in the chase but offering to the ancestral temple. Long neglected, what omission could be greater?
translations.idiomatic: An edict then stated: "Seasonal hunting follows established ritual regulations; this is not pleasure in the chase but offering to the ancestral temple. Long neglected, what omission could be greater?

sentences.zh: 爰遵時令，暫狩近郊，既躬獲禽，用以薦俎。

translations.literal: Following the season's command, we hunt briefly in the near suburbs; having personally taken game, it will be used for sacrificial stands.
translations.idiomatic: Following the season's command, we hunt briefly in the near suburbs; having personally taken game, it will be used for sacrificial stands.

sentences.zh: 其今月十一日畋 獵，親射所獲田禽，並付所司，以備太廟四時薦享，著為令。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of this month we hunt; the field birds personally shot are all entrusted to the responsible officials to supply the Imperial Ancestral Temple's four-season fresh offerings, established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of this month we hunt; the field birds personally shot are entrusted to the responsible officials to supply the Imperial Ancestral Temple's four-season fresh offerings, established as a regulation.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年，宗正丞趙良規言：“《通禮》著薦新凡五十餘物，今太廟祭享之外唯薦冰， 其餘薦新之禮，皆寢不行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court Zhao Lianggui stated: "The 'Comprehensive Rites' records more than fifty items for fresh offerings; now beyond the Imperial Ancestral Temple's sacrificial offerings only ice is presented, and the rest of the fresh-offering rites have all fallen into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyou (1035), Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court Zhao Lianggui reported: "The 'Comprehensive Rites' records more than fifty items for fresh offerings, yet beyond the Imperial Ancestral Temple's sacrificial offerings only ice is presented, and the rest of the fresh-offering rites have fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 宜以品物時新，所司送宗正，令尚食簡擇滋味與新物相宜者，配以薦之。

translations.literal: Seasonal fresh items should be sent by the responsible officials to the Imperial Clan Court; the imperial kitchen should select flavors matching the fresh items and pair them for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal fresh items should be sent by the responsible officials to the Imperial Clan Court, and the imperial kitchen should select flavors matching the fresh items and pair them for presentation.

sentences.zh: ”於是禮官、宗正條定：“逐室時薦，以京都新物，略依時訓， 協用典章。

translations.literal: " Thereupon ritual officials and the Imperial Clan Court specified: "For each chamber's seasonal presentation, use fresh items from the capital, roughly following seasonal instruction and conforming to canonical regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon ritual officials and the Imperial Clan Court specified that for each chamber's seasonal presentation fresh items from the capital should be used, roughly following seasonal instruction and conforming to canonical regulations.

sentences.zh: 請每歲春孟月薦蔬，以韭以菘，配以卵。

translations.literal: We request that each year in the first month of spring present vegetables — leeks and cabbage — paired with eggs.
translations.idiomatic: We request that each year in the first month of spring vegetables — leeks and cabbage — be presented, paired with eggs.

sentences.zh: 仲月薦冰，季月薦蔬以筍，果以含桃。

translations.literal: In the second month present ice; in the third month present bamboo shoots as vegetables and cherries as fruit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month ice should be presented; in the third month bamboo shoots as vegetables and cherries as fruit.

sentences.zh: 夏孟月嚐麥，配以彘，仲月薦果，以瓜以來禽，季月薦果，以芡以菱。

translations.literal: In the first month of summer taste wheat, paired with pork; in the second month present melons and field birds as fruit; in the third month present gorgon fruit and water caltrop.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of summer wheat should be tasted, paired with pork; in the second month melons and field birds should be presented as fruit; in the third month gorgon fruit and water caltrop.

sentences.zh: 秋 孟月嚐粟嚐穄，配以雞，果以棗以梨，仲月嚐酒嚐稻，蔬以筊筍，季月嚐豆嚐蕎麥。

translations.literal: In the first month of autumn taste millet and panicled millet, paired with chicken; jujubes and pears as fruit; in the second month taste wine and rice, water chestnuts and bamboo shoots as vegetables; in the third month taste beans and buckwheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of autumn millet and panicled millet should be tasted, paired with chicken, with jujubes and pears as fruit; in the second month wine and rice, with water chestnuts and bamboo shoots as vegetables; in the third month beans and buckwheat.

sentences.zh: 冬孟月羞以兔，果以栗，蔬以藇，仲月羞以雁以獐，季月羞以魚。

translations.literal: In the first month of winter present rabbit as delicacy, chestnuts as fruit, and calamus as vegetable; in the second month present geese and roe deer; in the third month present fish.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of winter rabbit should be presented as delicacy, chestnuts as fruit, and calamus as vegetable; in the second month geese and roe deer; in the third month fish.

sentences.zh: 凡二十八 種，所司烹治。

translations.literal: Twenty-eight kinds in all, prepared by the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-eight kinds in all, to be prepared by the responsible officials.

sentences.zh: 自彘以下，令禦廚於四時牙盤食烹饌，卜日薦獻，一如《開寶通禮》。

translations.literal: From pork onward, order the imperial kitchen to prepare four-season tooth-platter meals; choose an auspicious day for presentation, following the "Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao."
translations.idiomatic: From pork onward, the imperial kitchen should prepare four-season tooth-platter meals; an auspicious day should be chosen for presentation, following the "Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao."

sentences.zh: ”又太常禮院言：“自來薦冰，惟薦太廟逐室帝主，後主皆闕。

translations.literal: " The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Affairs also stated: "Hitherto ice offerings have been presented only to the imperial spirit tablets in each chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; empress spirit tablets have all been omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Affairs also reported that hitherto ice offerings had been presented only to the imperial spirit tablets in each chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, with empress spirit tablets omitted.

sentences.zh: 謹按朔望每室 牙盤食，帝後同薦。

translations.literal: We respectfully note that on new-moon and full-moon days each chamber receives tooth-platter food, with emperor and empress presented together.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully note that on new-moon and full-moon days each chamber receives tooth-platter food, with emperor and empress presented together.

sentences.zh: 又按《禮》：‘有薦新如朔奠。

translations.literal: We also note the "Rites": 'Fresh offerings are like new-moon offerings.
translations.idiomatic: We also note the "Rites": "Fresh offerings are like new-moon offerings.

sentences.zh: ’詳此獻祀，帝後主別無異等之義。

translations.literal: ' Examining these presentations, there is no principle of different rank between emperor and empress spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Examining these presentations, there is no principle of different rank between emperor and empress spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 今後前廟逐室後主，欲乞四時薦新，並如朔望牙盤例，後廟、奉慈廟如太廟 之禮。

translations.literal: Henceforth for empress spirit tablets in each chamber of the front temple, we request that four-season fresh offerings all follow the new-moon and full-moon tooth-platter precedent; the rear temple and Fengci Temple should follow the Imperial Ancestral Temple rites.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth for empress spirit tablets in each chamber of the front temple, we request that four-season fresh offerings follow the new-moon and full-moon tooth-platter precedent, and that the rear temple and Fengci Temple follow the Imperial Ancestral Temple rites.

sentences.zh: 皇祐三年，太常寺王洙言：“每內降新物，有司皆擇吉日，至涉三四日，而物已損敗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangyou, Wang Zhu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices stated: "Whenever fresh items arrive from the palace, the responsible officials all choose an auspicious day, taking three or four days, by which time the items have spoiled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangyou (1051), Wang Zhu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Whenever fresh items arrive from the palace, the responsible officials choose an auspicious day, taking three or four days, by which time the items have spoiled.

sentences.zh: 自今令禮部預為關報，於次日薦之，更不擇日。

translations.literal: From now on order the Ministry of Rites to give advance notice, presenting on the following day without choosing a date.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Ministry of Rites should give advance notice and present on the following day without choosing a date.

sentences.zh: 詳定所言：“古者薦新於廟之寢，無屍，不卜日，不出神主，奠而不祭。

translations.literal: The commission for determining rites stated: "In antiquity fresh offerings were made in the temple's sleeping chamber, with no impersonator, no date selection, no bringing out spirit tablets — presentation without sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The commission for determining rites stated: "In antiquity fresh offerings were made in the temple's sleeping chamber, with no impersonator, no date selection, and no bringing out spirit tablets — presentation without sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 近時擇日而薦，非也。

translations.literal: Recently choosing a date for presentation is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Recently choosing a date for presentation is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 天子諸侯，物熟則薦，不以孟仲季為限。

translations.literal: For the Son of Heaven and feudal lords, when items ripen they are presented, not limited to first, second, or third months.
translations.idiomatic: For the Son of Heaven and feudal lords, when items ripen they are presented, not limited to first, second, or third months of the season.

sentences.zh: 《呂氏•月令》，一歲之 間八薦新物，《開元禮》加以五十餘品。

translations.literal: Master Lü's "Monthly Ordinances" lists eight fresh items within a year; the "Kaiyuan Rites" adds more than fifty kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Master Lü's "Monthly Ordinances" lists eight fresh items within a year; the "Kaiyuan Rites" adds more than fifty kinds.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，禮官議以《呂紀》簡而近薄，唐令雜而不經，於是更定四時所薦凡二十八物，除依《詩》、《禮》、《月令》外， 又增多十有七品。

translations.literal: In Jingyou, ritual officials judged Master Lü's ordinances too simple and nearly inadequate, and Tang regulations too miscellaneous and uncanonical; they then fixed twenty-eight items for the four seasons, beyond those in the "Classic of Poetry," "Rites," and "Monthly Ordinances" adding seventeen more kinds.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou ritual officials judged Master Lü's ordinances too simple and nearly inadequate, and Tang regulations too miscellaneous and uncanonical. They then fixed twenty-eight items for the four seasons; beyond those in the "Classic of Poetry," "Rites," and "Monthly Ordinances" they added seventeen more kinds.

sentences.zh: 雖出一時之議，然歲時登薦，行之已久。

translations.literal: Although this arose from deliberation of one time, seasonal presentation has been practiced for long.
translations.idiomatic: Although this arose from deliberation of one time, seasonal presentation has long been practiced.

sentences.zh: 依於古則太略，違於經則無法。

translations.literal: Following antiquity would be too sparse; departing from the classics would leave no standard.
translations.idiomatic: Following antiquity would be too sparse; departing from the classics would leave no standard.

sentences.zh: 今欲稍加刊定，取其間先王所嚐享用膳羞之物，見於經者存之，不經者去 之。

translations.literal: We now wish to revise slightly, taking among them foods the former kings tasted and used as delicacies — keeping those found in the classics, removing those not.
translations.idiomatic: We now wish to revise slightly, keeping among them foods the former kings tasted and used as delicacies that appear in the classics and removing those that do not.

sentences.zh: 請自今孟春薦韭以卵，羞以葑，仲春薦冰，季春薦筍，羞以含桃；

translations.literal: We request that from now on in early spring present leeks with eggs, turnips as delicacy; in mid-spring present ice; in late spring present bamboo shoots, cherries as delicacy;
translations.idiomatic: We request that from now on in early spring leeks with eggs be presented and turnips as delicacy; in mid-spring ice; in late spring bamboo shoots and cherries as delicacy;

sentences.zh: 孟夏嚐麥以彘，仲夏嚐雛以黍，羞以瓜，季夏羞以芡以菱；

translations.literal: in early summer taste wheat with pork; in mid-summer taste chicks with millet, melons as delicacy; in late summer present gorgon fruit and water caltrop;
translations.idiomatic: in early summer wheat with pork; in mid-summer chicks with millet and melons as delicacy; in late summer gorgon fruit and water caltrop;

sentences.zh: 孟秋嚐粟與稷，羞以棗以梨，仲秋 嚐麻嚐稻，羞以蒲，季秋嚐菽，羞以兔以栗；

translations.literal: in early autumn taste millet and glutinous millet, jujubes and pears as delicacy; in mid-autumn taste hemp and rice, calamus as delicacy; in late autumn taste beans, rabbit and chestnuts as delicacy;
translations.idiomatic: in early autumn millet and glutinous millet, with jujubes and pears as delicacy; in mid-autumn hemp and rice, with calamus as delicacy; in late autumn beans, with rabbit and chestnuts as delicacy;

sentences.zh: 孟冬羞以雁，仲冬羞以麕，季冬羞以魚。

translations.literal: in early winter present geese; in mid-winter present roe deer; in late winter present fish.
translations.idiomatic: in early winter geese; in mid-winter roe deer; in late winter fish.

sentences.zh: 今春不薦鮪，誠為闕典。

translations.literal: Now spring does not present sturgeon — this is truly a lacuna in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: That spring does not present sturgeon is truly a lacuna in ritual.

sentences.zh: 請季春薦鮪，無則闕之。

translations.literal: We request presenting sturgeon in late spring; if unavailable, omit it.
translations.idiomatic: We request presenting sturgeon in late spring; if unavailable, it may be omitted.

sentences.zh: 舊有林檎、蕎麥、藇之 類，及季秋嚐酒，並合刪去。

translations.literal: Former items such as crabapple, buckwheat, and calamus, and tasting wine in late autumn, should all be deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Former items such as crabapple, buckwheat, and calamus, and tasting wine in late autumn, should all be deleted.

sentences.zh: 凡新物及時出者，即日登獻，既非正祭，則不當卜日。

translations.literal: All fresh items appearing in season should be presented the same day; since this is not a formal sacrifice, an auspicious day should not be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: All fresh items appearing in season should be presented the same day; since this is not a formal sacrifice, an auspicious day should not be chosen.

sentences.zh: 《漢儀》嚐韭之屬，皆於廟而不在寢，故《韋玄成傳》以為廟歲二十五祠，而薦 新在焉。

translations.literal: The "Han Ritual Compendium" states that tasting leeks and the like are all in the temple hall, not the sleeping chamber; thus Wei Xuancheng's biography holds that the temple has twenty-five sacrifices per year, fresh offerings among them.
translations.idiomatic: The "Han Ritual Compendium" states that tasting leeks and the like are all in the temple hall, not the sleeping chamber; thus Wei Xuancheng's biography holds that the temple has twenty-five sacrifices per year, with fresh offerings among them.

sentences.zh: 自漢至於隋、唐，因仍其失，薦新雖在廟，然皆不出神主。

translations.literal: From Han through Sui and Tang, this error continued; fresh offerings though in the temple hall still did not bring out spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: From Han through Sui and Tang this error continued; fresh offerings, though in the temple hall, still did not bring out spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 今出神主，失禮尤甚。

translations.literal: Now bringing out spirit tablets is an even graver breach of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Now bringing out spirit tablets is an even graver breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 請依《五禮精義》，但設神座，仍候廟成，薦新於寢。

translations.literal: We request following the "Essential Meaning of the Five Rites," setting only spirit seats, and when the temple is complete, making fresh offerings in the sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: We request following the "Essential Meaning of the Five Rites," setting only spirit seats, and when the temple is complete, making fresh offerings in the sleeping chamber.

sentences.zh: ”詔依所定，如鮪 闕，即以魴鯉代之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved the determination; if sturgeon is unavailable, bream and carp may substitute.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the determination; if sturgeon is unavailable, bream and carp may substitute.

sentences.zh: 既而知宗正丞趙彥若言：“禮院以仲秋茭萌不經，易以蒲白。

translations.literal: Subsequently Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court Zhao Yanruo stated: "The ritual commission replaced mid-autumn water-chestnut shoots, not found in the classics, with calamus root.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court Zhao Yanruo reported: "The ritual commission replaced mid-autumn water-chestnut shoots, not found in the classics, with calamus root.

sentences.zh: 今仲秋蒲無白，改從春獻。

translations.literal: Now in mid-autumn calamus has no white root; change to spring presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Now in mid-autumn calamus has no white root; presentation should be moved to spring.

sentences.zh: 大觀，禮局亦言：“薦新雖係以月，如 櫻、筍三月當進，或萌實未成，轉至孟夏之類，自當隨時之宜，取新以薦。

translations.literal: In Daguan, the Ritual Bureau also stated: "Fresh offerings though tied to months — if cherries and bamboo shoots due in the third month have buds or fruit not yet ripe, extending to early summer and the like — should naturally follow seasonal suitability and present what is fresh.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan the Ritual Bureau also stated: "Fresh offerings though tied to months — if cherries and bamboo shoots due in the third month have buds or fruit not yet ripe, extending to early summer and the like — should naturally follow seasonal suitability and present what is fresh.

sentences.zh: ”政和四年，比部員外郎何天衢言：“祭不欲數，數則煩，祭不欲疏，疏則怠。

translations.literal: " In the fourth year of Zhenghe, Supernumerary Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue He Tianqu stated: "Sacrifice should not be too frequent — frequent becomes burdensome; sacrifice should not be too sparse — sparse becomes negligent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenghe (1114), Supernumerary Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue He Tianqu reported: "Sacrifice should not be too frequent — frequent becomes burdensome; sacrifice should not be too sparse — sparse becomes negligent.

sentences.zh: 先王建祭 祀之禮，必得疏數之中，未聞一日之間，遂行兩祭者也。

translations.literal: The former kings established sacrificial ritual to achieve the mean between sparse and frequent; never has one heard of performing two sacrifices in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings established sacrificial ritual to achieve the mean between sparse and frequent; never has one heard of performing two sacrifices in a single day.

sentences.zh: 今太廟薦新，有與朔祭同日者。

translations.literal: Now Imperial Ancestral Temple fresh offerings sometimes fall on the same day as new-moon sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Now Imperial Ancestral Temple fresh offerings sometimes fall on the same day as new-moon sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 夫朔祭行於一月之首，不可易也。

translations.literal: The new-moon sacrifice is performed at the month's beginning and cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The new-moon sacrifice is performed at the month's beginning and cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 若夫薦新，則未嚐卜日，一月之內，皆可 薦也。

translations.literal: As for fresh offerings, no auspicious day has been chosen; within the month any day may serve for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: As for fresh offerings, no auspicious day has been chosen; within the month any day may serve for presentation.

sentences.zh: 新物未備，猶許次月薦之，亦何必同朔日哉？

translations.literal: If fresh items are not ready, presentation the next month is permitted — why must it coincide with the new-moon day?
translations.idiomatic: If fresh items are not ready, presentation the next month is permitted — why must it coincide with the new-moon day?

sentences.zh: ”自是薦新偶與朔祭同日，詔用次日焉。

translations.literal: " Henceforth when fresh offerings happen to coincide with new-moon sacrifice, an edict ordered using the following day.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth when fresh offerings happened to coincide with new-moon sacrifice, an edict ordered using the following day.

sentences.zh: 中興仍舊制。

translations.literal: After the restoration the old regulation continued.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration the old regulation continued.

sentences.zh: 加上祖宗諡號。

translations.literal: Adding posthumous titles of ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Adding Posthumous Titles of Ancestors

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆元年九月，太常禮 院言：“謹按唐大中初，追尊順宗、憲宗諡號，皇帝於宣政殿授玉冊，遣宰臣以下持節奉冊赴太廟。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jianlong under Emperor Taizu, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Affairs stated: "We respectfully note that in early Dazhong of Tang, posthumous titles were conferred on Emperor Shunzong and Emperor Xianzong; the emperor at the Xuanzheng Hall conferred jade registers and dispatched chief ministers and below bearing credentials to convey the registers to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Jianlong (960), during the reign of Emperor Taizu, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Affairs reported: "We respectfully note that in early Dazhong of Tang posthumous titles were conferred on Emperor Shunzong and Emperor Xianzong; the emperor at the Xuanzheng Hall conferred jade registers and dispatched chief ministers and below bearing credentials to convey the registers to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 授冊日，帝既禦殿，百僚拜訖，降階跪授冊於太尉，候太尉奉冊 出宣政門，然後升殿。

translations.literal: On the day of conferring the register, after the emperor had taken the hall and all officials bowed, he descended the steps, knelt, and handed the register to the grand marshal; when the grand marshal had conveyed the register out the Xuanzheng gate, he then ascended the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of conferring the register, after the emperor had taken the hall and all officials bowed, he descended the steps, knelt, and handed the register to the grand marshal; when the grand marshal had conveyed the register out the Xuanzheng gate, he then ascended the hall.

sentences.zh: 凡皇帝行禮，皆太常卿讚導奉引。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor performed rites, the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices announced and guided him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor performed rites, the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices announced and guided him.

sentences.zh: ”奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 是月二十七日，帝御崇元殿，備禮遣使奉冊上四廟諡號。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of that month, the emperor took the Chongyuan Hall, prepared the rites, and dispatched envoys to convey registers conferring posthumous titles on the four ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day of that month the emperor took the Chongyuan Hall, prepared the rites, and dispatched envoys to convey registers conferring posthumous titles on the four ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 皇帝高祖府君冊曰：“孝曾孫嗣皇帝臣 某，再拜稽首上言，伏以昊天有命，皇宋勃興，括厚載以開階，宅中區而撫運，夷夏蠻貊，罔不獻誠，山川鬼神，罔不受職。

translations.literal: The register for the emperor's great-great-grandfather states: "The filial great-great-grandson, succeeding emperor, your subject so-and-so, bowing twice and prostrating, submits: Humbly considering that August Heaven had a mandate, the Great Song rose vigorously, embracing the thick earth to open its foundation, dwelling in the central realm to govern fortune, barbarians of east and west and all Man tribes none failing to offer sincerity, mountains, rivers, and spirits none failing to accept their duties.
translations.idiomatic: The register for the emperor's great-great-grandfather states: "The filial great-great-grandson, succeeding emperor, your subject, bowing twice and prostrating, submits: Humbly considering that August Heaven had a mandate, the Great Song rose vigorously, embracing the thick earth to open its foundation, dwelling in the central realm to govern fortune, barbarians of east and west and all Man tribes none failing to offer sincerity, mountains, rivers, and spirits none failing to accept their duties.

sentences.zh: 非臣否德，肇此丕圖，實賴先正儲休， 上玄降鑒，既虔膺於大寶，乃眇覿於遐源，敢遵曆代之規，式薦配天之號。

translations.literal: It is not this subject's virtue that began this great design; truly it relies on forebears storing up blessing and the Supreme Mystery descending to observe. Having reverently received the great treasure, I now gaze upon distant origins and dare follow the regulations of successive ages to present a title matching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It is not this subject's virtue that began this great design; truly it relies on forebears storing up blessing and the Supreme Mystery descending to observe. Having reverently received the great treasure, I now gaze upon distant origins and dare follow the regulations of successive ages to present a title matching Heaven.

sentences.zh: 謹遣使司空兼門下侍郎同中書門下平章事王溥、副使兵部尚書李濤奉寶冊，上尊諡曰文獻 皇帝，廟號僖祖，皇帝高祖母崔氏曰文懿皇后。

translations.literal: Respectfully dispatching envoy Grand Marshal and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Administrator of the Secretariat-Chancellery Wang Pu, and deputy envoy Minister of War Li Tao, to convey the treasure register, conferring the honorific posthumous title Emperor Wenxian, temple name Emperor Xizu, and the emperor's great-great-grandmother Lady Cui as Empress Wanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully dispatching envoy Grand Marshal and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Administrator of the Secretariat-Chancellery Wang Pu, and deputy envoy Minister of War Li Tao, to convey the treasure register, conferring the honorific posthumous title Emperor Wenxian, temple name Emperor Xizu, and the emperor's great-great-grandmother Lady Cui as Empress Wanyi.

sentences.zh: ”皇曾祖府君冊曰：“伏以天命匪忱，惟歸於有德，人文設教，必始於貽謀。

translations.literal: " The register for the imperial great-grandfather states: "Humbly considering that Heaven's mandate is not constant but returns to the virtuous, and human culture establishes teaching, it must begin with bequeathed counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The register for the imperial great-grandfather states: "Humbly considering that Heaven's mandate is not constant but returns to the virtuous, and human culture establishes teaching, it must begin with bequeathed counsel.

sentences.zh: 乘時既肇於興王，報本敢稽於尊祖。

translations.literal: Seizing the time that began with the rise of kings, repaying the root I dare delay in honoring the revered ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the time that began with the rise of kings, repaying the root I dare delay in honoring the revered ancestor.

sentences.zh: 非 隆徽稱，則大享何以配神，非鏤良瑉，則洪烈何由垂世？

translations.literal: Without elevating the honorific title, how can the great offering match the spirits? Without inscribing on fine jade, how can the grand achievement be handed down through the ages?
translations.idiomatic: Without elevating the honorific title, how can the great offering match the spirits? Without inscribing on fine jade, how can the grand achievement be handed down through the ages?

sentences.zh: 方作《猗那》之頌，永嚴昭穆之容。

translations.literal: About to compose the hymn "How Grand," forever to solemnize the appearance of the ancestral line.
translations.idiomatic: About to compose the hymn "How Grand," forever to solemnize the appearance of the ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 謹遣使王溥、副使李濤奉冊寶，上尊諡曰惠元皇帝，廟號順祖，皇曾祖 母桑氏曰惠明皇后。

translations.literal: Respectfully dispatching envoy Wang Pu and deputy envoy Li Tao to convey the register and treasure, conferring the honorific posthumous title Emperor Huiyuan, temple name Emperor Shunzu, and the imperial great-grandmother Lady Sang as Empress Huiming.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully dispatching envoy Wang Pu and deputy envoy Li Tao to convey the register and treasure, conferring the honorific posthumous title Emperor Huiyuan, temple name Emperor Shunzu, and the imperial great-grandmother Lady Sang as Empress Huiming.

sentences.zh: ”皇祖驍衛府君冊曰：“伏以人瞻烏止，運葉龍飛。

translations.literal: " The register for the imperial grandfather, Commandant of the Brave Guards, states: "Humbly considering that men gaze where the crow rests and fortune's leaf flies like a dragon.
translations.idiomatic: The register for the imperial grandfather, Commandant of the Brave Guards, states: "Humbly considering that men gaze where the crow rests and fortune's leaf flies like a dragon.

sentences.zh: 非發源之長，析派不能通上漢；

translations.literal: Without a long source, branching streams cannot reach the upper Han;
translations.idiomatic: Without a long source, branching streams cannot reach the upper Han;

sentences.zh: 非積基之厚，嗣孫不能有中區。

translations.literal: without a thick foundation, succeeding descendants cannot possess the central realm.
translations.idiomatic: without a thick foundation, succeeding descendants cannot possess the central realm.

sentences.zh: 今人紀肇修，孝思罔極，酌 百王之損益，薦四廟之蒸嚐。

translations.literal: Now human records begin their compilation; filial thought knows no limit; weighing the additions and reductions of a hundred kings, presenting zheng and chang to the four temples.
translations.idiomatic: Now human records begin their compilation; filial thought knows no limit; weighing the additions and reductions of a hundred kings, presenting zheng and chang to the four temples.

sentences.zh: 謹遣使王溥、副使李濤奉寶冊，上尊諡曰簡恭皇帝，廟號翼祖，皇祖母京兆郡太夫人劉氏曰簡穆皇后。

translations.literal: Respectfully dispatching envoy Wang Pu and deputy envoy Li Tao to convey the treasure register, conferring the honorific posthumous title Emperor Jiangong, temple name Emperor Yizu, and the imperial grandmother Lady Liu, Grand Mistress of Jingzhao Commandery, as Empress Jianmu.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully dispatching envoy Wang Pu and deputy envoy Li Tao to convey the treasure register, conferring the honorific posthumous title Emperor Jiangong, temple name Emperor Yizu, and the imperial grandmother Lady Liu, Grand Mistress of Jingzhao Commandery, as Empress Jianmu.

sentences.zh: ”聖考太尉府君冊曰：“昔者流 火開祥，周發薦文王之號，黃星應運，曹丕揚魏祖之功。

translations.literal: " The register for the sacred father, Grand Marshal, states: "Formerly when the Fire Star opened auspicious signs, King Fa of Zhou presented King Wen's title; when the Yellow Star responded to fortune, Cao Pi proclaimed the Wei ancestor's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The register for the sacred father, Grand Marshal, states: "Formerly when the Fire Star opened auspicious signs, King Fa of Zhou presented King Wen's title; when the Yellow Star responded to fortune, Cao Pi proclaimed the Wei ancestor's achievement.

sentences.zh: 鹹因致孝之誠，式展尊親之義，爰遵大典，亟上尊稱。

translations.literal: All because of the sincerity of utmost filial piety, to display the principle of honoring parents, following the great rite, urgently presenting the honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: All because of the sincerity of utmost filial piety, to display the principle of honoring parents, following the great rite, urgently presenting the honorific title.

sentences.zh: 謹遣使王溥、副使李濤奉冊寶，上尊諡曰昭武皇帝， 廟號宣祖。

translations.literal: Respectfully dispatching envoy Wang Pu and deputy envoy Li Tao to convey the register and treasure, conferring the honorific posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu, temple name Emperor Xuanzu.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully dispatching envoy Wang Pu and deputy envoy Li Tao to convey the register and treasure, conferring the honorific posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu, temple name Emperor Xuanzu.

sentences.zh: ”禮畢，群臣進表奉慰。

translations.literal: " When the rites were finished, all officials submitted memorials of condolence.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, all officials submitted memorials of condolence.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國二年正月甲戌，上太祖英武聖文神德皇帝。

translations.literal: In the first month, day jiaxu, of the second year of Taiping Xingguo under Emperor Taizong, Emperor Taizu was given the title Emperor Yingwu Shengwen Shende.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, day jiaxu, of the second year of Taiping Xingguo (977), during the reign of Emperor Taizong, Emperor Taizu was given the title Emperor Yingwu Shengwen Shende.

sentences.zh: 真宗大中祥符元年十一月二十七日，帝於朝元殿備禮，奉 祖宗尊諡冊寶，再拜授攝太尉王旦奉之以出，安太祖冊寶於玉輅，太宗冊寶於金輅，詣太廟，奉上太祖曰啟運立極英武聖文神德玄功大孝皇帝，太宗曰至仁應道神功 聖德文武大明廣孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu under Emperor Zhenzong, the emperor at the Chaoyuan Hall prepared the rites, presented the honorific posthumous registers and treasures of the ancestors, bowed twice and handed them to Acting Grand Marshal Wang Dan to convey out; Emperor Taizu's register and treasure were placed on the jade chariot, Emperor Taizong's on the gold chariot; proceeding to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, presenting to Emperor Taizu the title Emperor Qiyun Liji Yingwu Shengwen Shende Xuangong Daxiao, and to Emperor Taizong Emperor Zhiren Yingdao Shengong Shengde Wenwu Daming Guangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1008), during the reign of Emperor Zhenzong, the emperor at the Chaoyuan Hall prepared the rites and presented the honorific posthumous registers and treasures of the ancestors. He bowed twice and handed them to Acting Grand Marshal Wang Dan to convey out. Emperor Taizu's register and treasure were placed on the jade chariot and Emperor Taizong's on the gold chariot. Proceeding to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he presented to Emperor Taizu the title Emperor Qiyun Liji Yingwu Shengwen Shende Xuangong Daxiao and to Emperor Taizong Emperor Zhiren Yingdao Shengong Shengde Wenwu Daming Guangxiao.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，親行朝享之禮。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, he personally performed the morning offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, he personally performed the morning offering rite.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年正月九日，加上六室尊諡二字：僖祖曰文獻睿和皇帝，順祖曰惠元睿明皇帝，翼祖曰簡恭睿德皇帝，宣祖曰 昭武睿聖皇帝，太祖曰啟運立極英武睿文神德聖功至明大孝皇帝，太宗曰至仁應道神功聖德睿烈大明廣孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the first month of the first year of Tianxi, two characters were added to the honorific posthumous titles of the six chambers: Emperor Xizu became Emperor Wenxian Ruihe, Emperor Shunzu Emperor Huiyuan Ruiming, Emperor Yizu Emperor Jiangong Ruide, Emperor Xuanzu Emperor Zhaowu Ruisheng, Emperor Taizu Emperor Qiyun Liji Yingwu Ruiwen Shende Shengong Zhiming Daxiao, and Emperor Taizong Emperor Zhiren Yingdao Shengong Shengde Ruilie Daming Guangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the first month in the first year of Tianxi (1017) two characters were added to the honorific posthumous titles of the six chambers: Emperor Xizu became Emperor Wenxian Ruihe, Emperor Shunzu Emperor Huiyuan Ruiming, Emperor Yizu Emperor Jiangong Ruide, Emperor Xuanzu Emperor Zhaowu Ruisheng, Emperor Taizu Emperor Qiyun Liji Yingwu Ruiwen Shende Shengong Zhiming Daxiao, and Emperor Taizong Emperor Zhiren Yingdao Shengong Shengde Ruilie Daming Guangxiao.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，群臣拜表稱賀。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, all officials submitted memorials of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, all officials submitted memorials of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 十一日，帝行朝享之禮。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day, the emperor performed the morning offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day the emperor performed the morning offering rite.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖二年十一月二十五日，加上真宗諡曰文明武定章聖元孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month of the second year of Tiansheng under Emperor Renzong, Emperor Zhenzong's posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Wenming Wuding Zhangsheng Yuanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month in the second year of Tiansheng (1024), during the reign of Emperor Renzong, Emperor Zhenzong's posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Wenming Wuding Zhangsheng Yuanxiao.

sentences.zh: 慶曆七年十一月二十五日，加上真宗諡曰膺符稽古成功讓德文明武定章聖元孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month of the seventh year of Qingli, Emperor Zhenzong's posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Yingfu Jigu Chenggong Rangde Wenming Wuding Zhangsheng Yuanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month in the seventh year of Qingli (1047) Emperor Zhenzong's posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Yingfu Jigu Chenggong Rangde Wenming Wuding Zhangsheng Yuanxiao.

sentences.zh: 神宗元豐六年五月，改加上尊諡作奉上徽號。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Shenzong, the term for adding honorific posthumous titles was changed to presenting honorific epithets.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Yuanfeng (1083), during the reign of Emperor Shenzong, the term for adding honorific posthumous titles was changed to presenting honorific epithets.

sentences.zh: 十一月二日，奉上仁宗徽號曰體天法道極功全德神文聖武睿哲明孝皇帝，又上英宗徽號曰體乾膺曆隆功盛德憲文肅武睿神宣孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On the second day of the eleventh month, the honorific epithet presented for Emperor Renzong was Emperor Titian Fadao Jigong Quande Shenwen Shengwu Ruizhe Mingxiao; the honorific epithet for Emperor Yingzong was Emperor Tiqian Yingli Longgong Shengde Xianwen Suwu Ruishen Xuanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the eleventh month the honorific epithet presented for Emperor Renzong was Emperor Titian Fadao Jigong Quande Shenwen Shengwu Ruizhe Mingxiao, and the honorific epithet for Emperor Yingzong was Emperor Tiqian Yingli Longgong Shengde Xianwen Suwu Ruishen Xuanxiao.

sentences.zh: 哲宗紹聖二年正月，帝謂輔臣曰：“祖宗諡號，各加至十六字。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Shaosheng under Emperor Zhezong, the emperor told his chief ministers: "The posthumous titles of the ancestors have each been augmented to sixteen characters.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Shaosheng (1095), during the reign of Emperor Zhezong, the emperor told his chief ministers: "The posthumous titles of the ancestors have each been augmented to sixteen characters.

sentences.zh: 神宗皇帝今止初諡，尚未增加，宜考求典故以聞。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong now has only his initial posthumous title and has not yet received augmentation; precedent should be investigated and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong now has only his initial posthumous title and has not yet received augmentation; precedent should be investigated and reported.

sentences.zh: ”宰臣章惇等對曰：“祖宗加諡，歲月不定。

translations.literal: " Chief Minister Zhang Dun and others replied: "Augmentation of ancestors' posthumous titles has no fixed interval.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Dun and others replied: "Augmentation of ancestors' posthumous titles has no fixed interval.

sentences.zh: 真 廟初加八字，是天聖二年。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong's first augmentation of eight characters was in the second year of Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong's first augmentation of eight characters was in the second year of Tiansheng.

sentences.zh: 今神宗祔廟已十年，故事加徽號必在南郊前，謹如聖旨討閱以聞。

translations.literal: Now ten years have passed since Emperor Shenzong was enshrined in the temple; by precedent honorific epithets are added before the Southern Suburb sacrifice; we respectfully follow the imperial command to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Now ten years have passed since Emperor Shenzong was enshrined in the temple; by precedent honorific epithets are added before the Southern Suburb sacrifice. We respectfully follow the imperial command to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: ”四月二十七日，詔加上神宗皇帝徽號，於大禮前三日行禮。

translations.literal: " On the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month, an edict ordered augmentation of Emperor Shenzong's honorific epithet, with the rite performed three days before the grand ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month an edict ordered augmentation of Emperor Shenzong's honorific epithet, with the rite performed three days before the grand ceremony.

sentences.zh: 九月十六 日，奉上冊寶曰神宗紹天法古運德建功英文烈武欽仁聖孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the ninth month, the register and treasure were presented with the honorific epithet Emperor Shenzong Shaotian Fagu Yunde Jiangong Yingwen Liewu Qinren Shengxiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day of the ninth month the register and treasure were presented with the honorific epithet Emperor Shenzong Shaotian Fagu Yunde Jiangong Yingwen Liewu Qinren Shengxiao.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年十一月，詔議加上徽宗徽號曰體神合道駿烈遜功聖文仁 德憲慈顯孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year of Shaoxing, an edict ordered deliberation on augmenting Emperor Huizong's honorific epithet to Emperor Tishen Hedao Junlie Xungong Shengwen Rendé Xianci Xianxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year of Shaoxing (1142) an edict ordered deliberation on augmenting Emperor Huizong's honorific epithet to Emperor Tishen Hedao Junlie Xungong Shengwen Rendé Xianci Xianxiao.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月九日，皇帝御文德殿，命宰臣秦檜奏請太廟。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the first month of the thirteenth year, the emperor took the Wende Hall and ordered Chief Minister Qin Hui to report the request to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the first month in the thirteenth year (1143) the emperor took the Wende Hall and ordered Chief Minister Qin Hui to report the request to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 十日，內殿宿齋，文武百僚集於發冊寶殿門幕次，次禮儀使、閣門官、太常博士、禮直官 分立禦幄前，次分引百僚入就殿下，東西相向立定，禮直官引奉冊寶使、侍中、中書令、舉寶舉冊官詣殿下西階之西，東向立。

translations.literal: On the tenth day, fasting overnight in the inner hall, civil and military officials gathered at the side pavilion of the Register-and-Treasure Presentation Hall gate; next the master of ceremonies, gate officials, doctors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and ritual supervisors stood separately before the imperial canopy; next they led officials in to take position below the hall, facing each other east and west; the ritual supervisor led the register-and-treasure envoy, palace attendant, director of the Secretariat, and officials bearing register and treasure to the west of the west steps below the hall, standing facing east.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day, after fasting overnight in the inner hall, civil and military officials gathered at the side pavilion of the Register-and-Treasure Presentation Hall gate. The master of ceremonies, gate officials, doctors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and ritual supervisors stood separately before the imperial canopy, then led officials in to take position below the hall facing each other east and west. The ritual supervisor led the register-and-treasure envoy, palace attendant, director of the Secretariat, and officials bearing register and treasure to the west of the west steps below the hall, standing facing east.

sentences.zh: 俟齋室簾降，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗 袍，禮部侍郎奏中嚴外辦。

translations.literal: When the fasting chamber curtain was lowered, the emperor wore the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe; the vice minister of rites reported mid-watch strictness and outer preparations.
translations.idiomatic: When the fasting chamber curtain was lowered, the emperor wore the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, and the vice minister of rites reported mid-watch strictness and outer preparations.

sentences.zh: 次禮直官、太常博士引禮儀使當幄前俯伏跪奏：“禮儀使臣某言，請皇帝行奉上徽宗皇帝發冊寶之禮。

translations.literal: Next the ritual supervisor and doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the master of ceremonies before the canopy to prostrate and kneel, reporting: "Your subject, master of ceremonies so-and-so, requests that the emperor perform the rite of presenting the register and treasure for Emperor Huizong.
translations.idiomatic: Next the ritual supervisor and doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the master of ceremonies before the canopy to prostrate and kneel, reporting: "Your subject, master of ceremonies, requests that the emperor perform the rite of presenting the register and treasure for Emperor Huizong.

sentences.zh: ”奏訖，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: " When the report was finished, he prostrated himself and rose.
translations.idiomatic: When the report was finished, he prostrated himself and rose.

sentences.zh: 簾卷，前導官 前導皇帝出幄，執大圭，詣冊寶幄東褥位，西向立，禮儀使奏請再拜，皇帝再拜，三上香，再拜，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: The curtain rolled up; the lead guide led the emperor out of the canopy, holding the great scepter, proceeding to the east mat position of the register-and-treasure canopy, standing facing west; the master of ceremonies requested a double bow; the emperor bowed twice, offered incense three times, bowed twice again, and all officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The curtain rolled up. The lead guide led the emperor out of the canopy, holding the great scepter, to the east mat position of the register-and-treasure canopy, standing facing west. The master of ceremonies requested a double bow; the emperor bowed twice, offered incense three times, bowed twice again, and all officials in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 前導還褥位，西向立，侍中、中書令、舉冊舉寶官 升殿，入冊寶幄。

translations.literal: The lead guide returned to the mat position, standing facing west; the palace attendant, director of the Secretariat, and officials bearing register and treasure ascended the hall and entered the register-and-treasure canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The lead guide returned to the mat position, standing facing west. The palace attendant, director of the Secretariat, and officials bearing register and treasure ascended the hall and entered the register-and-treasure canopy.

sentences.zh: 舉冊寶官俱搢笏跪，舉冊寶與侍中、中書令奉冊寶進行，皇帝後從，降自西階，至殿下褥位，南向立。

translations.literal: The officials bearing register and treasure all tucked their tablets and knelt, lifting register and treasure; with the palace attendant and director of the Secretariat they conveyed the register and treasure forward; the emperor followed behind, descended the west steps, reached the mat position below the hall, and stood facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The officials bearing register and treasure all tucked their tablets and knelt and lifted the register and treasure. With the palace attendant and director of the Secretariat they conveyed the register and treasure forward; the emperor followed behind, descended the west steps, reached the mat position below the hall, and stood facing south.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏皇帝再拜，舉冊官奉冊，舉寶官奉 寶，皇帝搢大圭，跪奉受冊寶使，皇帝執大圭再拜，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies reported that the emperor should bow twice; the register-bearer presented the register and the treasure-bearer presented the treasure; the emperor tucked the great scepter, knelt, and presented them to the register-and-treasure envoy; the emperor took the great scepter and bowed twice, and all officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies reported that the emperor should bow twice. The register-bearer presented the register and the treasure-bearer presented the treasure. The emperor tucked the great scepter, knelt, and presented them to the register-and-treasure envoy, then took the great scepter and bowed twice; all officials in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 持節者持節導冊寶進行，出殿正門。

translations.literal: Those bearing credentials held them and guided the register and treasure forward, exiting the main hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: Those bearing credentials held them and guided the register and treasure forward, exiting the main hall gate.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏禮畢。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies reported that the rites were complete.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies reported that the rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 皇帝釋大圭，升自東階，入齋室。

translations.literal: The emperor released the great scepter, ascended the east steps, and entered the fasting chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released the great scepter, ascended the east steps, and entered the fasting chamber.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中 奏解嚴。

translations.literal: The director of the Ministry of Rites reported the lifting of strictness.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the Ministry of Rites reported the lifting of strictness.

sentences.zh: 次冊寶出北宮門，奉冊寶使以下騎從，至太廟靈星門外下馬，步從至太廟南神門外。

translations.literal: Next the register and treasure exited the North Palace gate; the register-and-treasure envoy and below rode in attendance; at the outer Lingxing gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple they dismounted and walked in attendance to the outer south spirit gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Next the register and treasure exited the North Palace gate. The register-and-treasure envoy and his party rode in attendance; at the outer Lingxing gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple they dismounted and walked in attendance to the outer south spirit gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 次日，文武百僚集於太廟幕次，分引詣殿下再拜，冊寶使詣各室行奠獻 禮。

translations.literal: The next day, civil and military officials gathered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple side pavilion; they were led in groups to bow twice below the hall; the register-and-treasure envoy proceeded to each chamber to perform the presentation rite.
translations.idiomatic: The next day civil and military officials gathered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple side pavilion, were led in groups to bow twice below the hall, and the register-and-treasure envoy proceeded to each chamber to perform the presentation rite.

sentences.zh: 次讚者引舉冊官舉冊，舉寶官舉寶，禮直官引侍中、中書令前導冊寶入自南正門，至殿西階下權置定，各再拜。

translations.literal: Next the announcer led the register-bearer to lift the register and the treasure-bearer to lift the treasure; the ritual supervisor led the palace attendant and director of the Secretariat to guide the register and treasure in through the south main gate; they were provisionally set below the west steps of the hall; all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Next the announcer led the register-bearer to lift the register and the treasure-bearer to lift the treasure. The ritual supervisor led the palace attendant and director of the Secretariat to guide the register and treasure in through the south main gate; they were provisionally set below the west steps of the hall, and all bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 次詣徽宗室，冊寶使俯伏跪奏稱：“嗣皇帝臣 某，謹遣臣等奉徽號冊寶。

translations.literal: Next proceeding to Emperor Huizong's chamber, the register-and-treasure envoy prostrated and knelt, reporting: "The succeeding emperor, your subject so-and-so, respectfully dispatches your subjects to present the honorific epithet register and treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Next proceeding to Emperor Huizong's chamber, the register-and-treasure envoy prostrated and knelt, reporting: "The succeeding emperor, your subject, respectfully dispatches your subjects to present the honorific epithet register and treasure.

sentences.zh: ”奉訖，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: " When the presentation was finished, he prostrated himself and rose.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentation was finished, he prostrated himself and rose.

sentences.zh: 舉冊官舉冊進，中書令跪讀冊文，舉寶官舉寶進，侍中跪讀寶文，冊寶使以下各再拜，至冊寶幄安奉。

translations.literal: The register-bearer lifted the register and advanced; the director of the Secretariat knelt and read the register text; the treasure-bearer lifted the treasure and advanced; the palace attendant knelt and read the treasure text; the register-and-treasure envoy and below each bowed twice; they proceeded to the register-and-treasure canopy and installed them reverently.
translations.idiomatic: The register-bearer lifted the register and advanced, and the director of the Secretariat knelt and read the register text. The treasure-bearer lifted the treasure and advanced, and the palace attendant knelt and read the treasure text. The register-and-treasure envoy and his party each bowed twice, then proceeded to the register-and-treasure canopy and installed them reverently.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，以次 退。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, they withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, they withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 次文武百僚奉表稱賀。

translations.literal: Next civil and military officials submitted memorials of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Next civil and military officials submitted memorials of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年八月，詔上高宗徽號曰受命中興全功至德聖神武文昭仁憲孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Shaoxi, an edict presented Emperor Gaozong's honorific epithet as Emperor Shouming Zhongxing Quangong Zhide Shenshen Wuwen Zhaoren Xianxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Shaoxi (1191) an edict presented Emperor Gaozong's honorific epithet as Emperor Shouming Zhongxing Quangong Zhide Shenshen Wuwen Zhaoren Xianxiao.

sentences.zh: 慶元三年，上孝宗徽號曰紹統同道冠德昭功哲文 神武明聖成孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingyuan, Emperor Xiaozong's honorific epithet was presented as Emperor Shaotong Tongdao Guande Zhaogong Zhewen Shenwu Mingsheng Chengxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qingyuan (1197) Emperor Xiaozong's honorific epithet was presented as Emperor Shaotong Tongdao Guande Zhaogong Zhewen Shenwu Mingsheng Chengxiao.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年，上光宗徽號曰循道憲仁明功茂德溫文順武聖哲慈孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiatai, Emperor Guangzong's honorific epithet was presented as Emperor Xundao Xianren Minggong Maode Wenwen Shunwu Shengzhé Cixiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiatai (1203) Emperor Guangzong's honorific epithet was presented as Emperor Xundao Xianren Minggong Maode Wenwen Shunwu Shengzhé Cixiao.

sentences.zh: 寶慶三年，上寧宗徽號曰法天備道純德茂功仁文哲武聖睿恭孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoqing, Emperor Ningzong's honorific epithet was presented as Emperor Fatian Beidao Chunde Maogong Renwen Zhewu Shengrui Gongxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoqing (1227) Emperor Ningzong's honorific epithet was presented as Emperor Fatian Beidao Chunde Maogong Renwen Zhewu Shengrui Gongxiao.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳二 年，上理宗徽號曰建道備德大功復興烈文仁武聖明安孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianchun, Emperor Lizong's honorific epithet was presented as Emperor Jiandao Beide Dagong Fuxing Liewen Renwu Shengming Anxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianchun (1266) Emperor Lizong's honorific epithet was presented as Emperor Jiandao Beide Dagong Fuxing Liewen Renwu Shengming Anxiao.

sentences.zh: 並如紹興十三年儀注。

translations.literal: All followed the ritual regulations of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: All followed the ritual regulations of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 廟諱。

translations.literal: Temple taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Temple Taboos

sentences.zh: 紹興二年十一月，禮部、太常寺言：“淵聖皇帝御名，見於 經傳義訓者，或以威武為義，或以回旋為義，又為植立之象，又為亭郵表名，又為圭名，又為姓氏，又為木名，當各以其義類求之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Shaoxing, the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices stated: "The personal name of Emperor Yuansheng, where it appears in classics and commentaries with defined meanings, sometimes carries the meaning of majesty and martial prowess, sometimes the meaning of turning and revolving, also the image of standing upright, also the name of a postal pavilion, also the name of a jade tablet, also a surname, and also the name of a tree — each should be sought according to its semantic category.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Shaoxing (1132) the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "The personal name of Emperor Yuansheng, where it appears in classics and commentaries with defined meanings, sometimes carries the meaning of majesty and martial prowess, sometimes the meaning of turning and revolving, also the image of standing upright, also the name of a postal pavilion, also the name of a jade tablet, also a surname, and also the name of a tree — each should be sought according to its semantic category.

sentences.zh: 以威武為義者，今欲讀曰‘威 ’；

translations.literal: Where the meaning is majesty and martial prowess, we now wish to read it as 'wei';
translations.idiomatic: Where the meaning is majesty and martial prowess, we now wish to read it as "wei";

sentences.zh: 以回旋為義者，今欲讀曰‘旋’；

translations.literal: where the meaning is turning and revolving, we now wish to read it as 'xuan';
translations.idiomatic: where the meaning is turning and revolving, we now wish to read it as "xuan";

sentences.zh: 以植立為義者，今欲讀曰‘植’；

translations.literal: where the meaning is standing upright, we now wish to read it as 'zhi';
translations.idiomatic: where the meaning is standing upright, we now wish to read it as "zhi";

sentences.zh: 若姓氏之類，欲去‘木’為‘亙’。

translations.literal: for categories such as surnames, we wish to remove 'mu' and use 'geng'.
translations.idiomatic: for categories such as surnames, we wish to remove "mu" and use "geng."

sentences.zh: 又緣漢法，‘邦’之字曰‘國’，‘盈’之字曰‘滿 ’，止是讀曰‘國’、曰‘滿’，其本字見於經傳者未嚐改易。

translations.literal: Furthermore, by Han law, the taboo form of 'bang' was 'guo' and of 'ying' was 'man' — one only read them as 'guo' and 'man'; the original characters appearing in classics were never altered.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, by Han law the taboo form of "bang" was "guo" and of "ying" was "man" — one only read them as "guo" and "man"; the original characters appearing in classics were never altered.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷，漢人也，作《史記》，曰：‘先王之製，邦內畿服，邦外侯服。

translations.literal: Sima Qian, a man of Han, wrote the "Records of the Grand Historian," saying: 'The former kings' regulation: within the domain was the inner service, outside the domain the outer service.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian, a man of Han, wrote the "Records of the Grand Historian," saying: "The former kings' regulation: within the domain was the inner service, outside the domain the outer service.

sentences.zh: ’又曰：‘盈而不持則傾。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'Full but not sustained, then it topples.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Full but not sustained, then it topples.

sentences.zh: ’於‘邦’字、‘盈’字亦不改易。

translations.literal: ' For the characters 'bang' and 'ying' he likewise did not alter them.
translations.idiomatic: For the characters "bang" and "ying" he likewise did not alter them.

sentences.zh: 今來淵聖皇帝御名，欲定讀如前外，其經傳本字，即不當改易，庶幾萬世之下，有所考證，推求義類，別無未盡。

translations.literal: Now regarding Emperor Yuansheng's personal name, beyond fixing the readings as above, the original characters in classics should not be altered, so that ten thousand generations hence there may be evidence for verification; searching semantic categories, nothing else remains unaddressed.
translations.idiomatic: Now regarding Emperor Yuansheng's personal name, beyond fixing the readings as above, the original characters in classics should not be altered, so that ten thousand generations hence there may be evidence for verification. Searching semantic categories, nothing else remains unaddressed.

sentences.zh: ”三十二年正 月，禮部、太常寺言：“欽宗祔廟，翼祖當遷。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the thirty-second year, the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices stated: "With Emperor Qinzong enshrined in the temple, Emperor Yizu should be moved.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirty-second year (1162) the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "With Emperor Qinzong enshrined in the temple, Emperor Yizu should be moved.

sentences.zh: 於正月九日，先遷翼祖皇帝、簡穆皇后神主奉藏於夾室。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the first month, first move the spirit tablets of Emperor Yizu and Empress Jianmu and reverently store them in the side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the first month the spirit tablets of Emperor Yizu and Empress Jianmu should first be moved and reverently stored in the side chamber.

sentences.zh: 所有以後翼祖皇帝諱，依禮不諱。

translations.literal: Henceforth Emperor Yizu's taboo name, according to ritual, need not be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth Emperor Yizu's taboo name, according to ritual, need not be avoided.

sentences.zh: ”詔恭依。

translations.literal: " An edict respectfully approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict respectfully approved.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年四月，詔：“今後臣庶命名，並不許犯祧廟正諱。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Shaoxi, an edict stated: "Henceforth when officials and commoners choose names, they must not violate the primary taboos of the distant ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Shaoxi (1190) an edict stated: "Henceforth when officials and commoners choose names, they must not violate the primary taboos of the distant ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 如名字見有犯祧廟正諱者，並合改易。

translations.literal: If names are found to violate the primary taboos of the distant ancestral temple, all should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: If names are found to violate the primary taboos of the distant ancestral temple, all should be changed.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年十月，司農寺丞岳珂言：“孝宗舊諱從‘伯’從‘玉’從‘宗’。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year of Jiading, Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Yue Ke stated: "Emperor Xiaozong's old taboo character is composed of 'bo,' 'yu,' and 'zong.'
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year of Jiading (1220) Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Yue Ke reported: "Emperor Xiaozong's old taboo character is composed of 'bo,' 'yu,' and 'zong.'

sentences.zh: 考國朝之製，祖宗舊諱二字者，皆著令不許並用。

translations.literal: Examining our dynasty's regulations, for ancestors' old two-character taboos, all are entered in regulations forbidding joint use.
translations.idiomatic: Examining our dynasty's regulations, for ancestors' old two-character taboos all are entered in regulations forbidding joint use.

sentences.zh: ”又言“欽宗舊諱二字，其一從 ‘[B08A]’從‘旦’，其一從‘火’從‘亙’，皆合回避。

translations.literal: " He also stated: "Emperor Qinzong's two old taboo characters — one composed of 'sun' and 'dan,' one of 'fire' and 'geng' — all should be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: He also stated that Emperor Qinzong's two old taboo characters — one composed of "sun" and "dan," one of "fire" and "geng" — all should be avoided.

sentences.zh: 乞並下禮、寺討論，頒降施行。

translations.literal: We request that both the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices be ordered to deliberate and promulgate for enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: We request that both the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices be ordered to deliberate and promulgate for enforcement.

sentences.zh: ”既而禮、寺討論：“所有欽宗、孝宗舊諱，若二字連用，並合回 避，宜從本官所請，刊入施行。

translations.literal: " Subsequently the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated: "For all old taboos of Emperors Qinzong and Xiaozong, if the two characters are used together, all should be avoided; the request of the submitting official should be followed and entered into enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated that for all old taboos of Emperors Qinzong and Xiaozong, if the two characters are used together all should be avoided; the request of the submitting official should be followed and entered into enforcement.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.
